When you arrive in Spain for education, Erasmus, a master's degree, or a doctorate, something else awaits you before paella and sangria: Spanish bureaucracy. 📂

The concepts of NIE and TIE are particularly confusing for newcomers to the country. Many people think they are the same thing, but not knowing the difference can hinder processes like opening a bank account or signing a contract.

In this article, we'll leave aside bureaucratic jargon and explain step-by-step how things work in real life, the most common mistakes, and how to obtain your Tie Immigration Certificate (TIE). Ready? Let's begin! 👇

🆔 1. What is NIE? (Identification Number)

NIE ( Número de Identidad de Extranjero ) is your foreign identity number in Spain. Think of it like your Turkish Republic Identity Number (TC Kimlik Numarası). The Spanish government identifies you using this number.

  • Characteristic: It starts with "Y" or "Z", continues with numbers, and ends with a letter (e.g., Y-1234567-R).

  • Where is it used? You need this number to open a bank account, get internet access, rent a house, pay bills, receive packages, and register for university.

⚠️ Important Note: NIE is just a number. It does not grant you residency rights on its own, nor is it a physical card. This number is usually printed on your visa (see "Numero de Identident" section).

🪪 2. What is TIE? (Physical Card)

TIE ( Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero ) is a physical residence permit card that you carry in your wallet. It is a plastic card containing your photo, fingerprints, address, and NIE number.

In short, the difference is this:

  • NIE: This is your number (like your name, it doesn't change).

  • TIE: That's the plastic card bearing that number (like your ID card, it gets replaced when it expires).

🤔 Who is required to obtain a TIE (Residence Permit)?

  • 🎓 Erasmus students (if they will be staying longer than 6 months).

  • 📚 Undergraduate, Master's and Doctoral students.

  • 🔬 Researchers and academics.

  • 📅 Long-term interns.

📝 Step-by-Step TIE Application Process

After entering Spain with a D-type student visa, you are legally required to initiate the application process for a TIE card within the first month . Here are the steps:

Step 1: Address Registration (Empadronamiento)

Before going to the police, you must go to your local municipality and register your address. This is called an "Empadronamiento". This document is required for your TIE appointment.

Step 2: Date Hunt (Cita Previa)

This is the most difficult part. You need to make an appointment with the immigration office ( Extranjeria ) or the police.

  • You must select the "Policia - Toma de Huella" (Fingerprint) option from the system.

  • Appointments open early in the morning and sell out in seconds. Be patient and keep trying.

Step 4: Required Documents

When your appointment (Cita) day arrives, you should have the following with you:

  1. Passport: Original and photocopy of the page with photo + visa page.

  2. Application Form (EX-17): Completed and signed.

  3. Photograph: One biometric photograph taken against a white background (ICAO standards).

  4. Empadronamiento: Address registration document obtained from the municipality (dated within the last 3 months).

  5. School Acceptance Letter: Matricula (University registration document).

  6. Appointment Slip: Printout of the appointment slip.

❌ 5 Most Common Mistakes

Mistakes that cause students to prolong the process:

  1. Don't Forget the Photocopies: Spanish officials love paper. Be sure to bring photocopies of every document with you.

  2. Incorrect Form Completion: The EX-17 form is required for TIE; do not confuse it with another form.

  3. Going Without an Appointment: Don't worry about whether they'll let you in at the door; it's impossible to get in without an appointment.

  4. Passport Expiration Date: They will not process your application if your passport is about to expire.

  5. Confusing NIE and TIE: It's a big mistake to think you don't need a card just because your visa says NIE. That's just your number; you have to get the card.

⏳ How long does it take to get a TIE card?

  • Appointment Scheduling: This can take anywhere from one week to two months, depending on the city.

  • Card Printing: Takes 30 to 45 days after fingerprinting.

  • Total time: It may take 2-3 months from the moment you arrive in Spain until you receive the card.

💡 Tip: Until your card is issued, the "Resguardo" (stamped document) you are given is your legal residence permit. However, you cannot leave Spain (outside the Schengen area) and return with this document. Plan your trip accordingly!

Conclusion: No Panic, There's a Plan

The residency permit process in Spain is a bit of a test of patience. However, if you have all the necessary documents and know what you're doing, there's nothing to fear.

Once you receive your TIE card, you will have full legal status within Spain, allowing you to travel and enjoy life.

A common complaint among foreigners living in France is: "No appointments available, the system is locked, nobody is answering."

If you're having trouble finding a titular séjour appointment, you're not alone. This isn't personal; it's entirely systemic. However, those who mismanage the process take unnecessary risks.

In this article, I explain methods that actually work, step by step and clearly.

❓ Why are there no Appointment Titles for Stay?

First, we must accept the truth: the prefecture system in France is inadequate.

The main reasons for this are: The number of immigrants is too high 🌍 There is insufficient staff 👥 The digital infrastructure is outdated 💻 The file prioritization system is not clear ⚠️

Especially in areas like Paris, Nanterre, Bobigny, and Créteil, appointments sell out in seconds. You go to the website and see the message "aucun créneau disponible" (no appointments available).

This is not your fault.

⏰ Realistic Timings for Scheduling Appointments

Many people check randomly throughout the day, but appointments usually open at specific times.

Very early in the morning ☀️ Late at night 🌙 Midday on weekdays, rarely

Using a computer instead of a phone is healthier. It's necessary to refresh the browser frequently and try it on different days.

To take one look and then give up is the biggest mistake.

💻 Online Application and File Upload Options

Many people don't know this, but some prefectures accept online applications without an appointment.

You may see the following options: Première demande en ligne, Renouvellement en ligne, Dépôt de dossier sans rendez-vous

Uploading files from these channels is very important. Even if you don't have an appointment, it leaves a trace of your application.

In France, the system only checks whether an application has been submitted or not.

📩 If you can't find an appointment, please send an email.

This section is critically important.

If you cannot get an appointment and your session is about to expire, you need to send an official email to the prefecture.

The email should include the following: A brief and clear explanation of your situation; a statement indicating that you were unable to get an appointment; and information that the necessary documents are ready.

This email constitutes legal evidence.

After sending the email, be sure to take a screenshot 📸 Make sure to include the date and time. Keep a copy of the email.

This will protect you.

⚖️ What happens if the session expires?

This is the most feared but also the most misunderstood topic.

If your residency permit has expired but you can prove you tried to schedule an appointment or submitted an application, you will usually not be penalized or subjected to deportation proceedings.

In France, what matters is a good-faith application. Doing nothing and waiting is a great risk.

🚫 The Most Common Mistakes

These errors put many files unnecessarily at risk.

Saying "I'll check when the system is up and running" and waiting for months ❌ Never sending emails ❌ Preparing incomplete documents ❌ Believing every piece of information in social media groups ❌

Remember. The prefecture sees your file, not your intentions.

📂 Your file should always be ready.

If an appointment comes up suddenly and you're unprepared, you miss the opportunity.

Documents you need to have ready: Passport 🛂 Current residence permit 🪪 School certificate or employment contract 📄 Proof of address 🏠 Insurance certificate ❤️🩹

If the file is ready, you can process the appointment within minutes.

🧠 Realistic Advice

The titre de séjour process requires patience. Getting angry or blaming the system won't change anything.

But these things make a difference: Keep trying; Do everything in writing; Keep evidence; Show that you've started the process.

France works slowly, but it doesn't forgive those who leave no trace.

📌 If you can't find a Titre de séjour appointment, it's not your fault. However, taking no action is a serious risk.

The correct approach is this: Regularly check your appointment pages. Use online application options. Definitely send an email and keep proof.

These three steps will protect you from many problems.

Moving to Spain for studies or an internship is an exciting process. But after packing your suitcase and dealing with the visa stress , the first bureaucratic hurdle upon arrival in Spain is usually opening a bank account. ✈️

A local IBAN (starting with ES) for rent payments, tuition fees, the expected Erasmus grant, or internship salary is not only practical but often essential. However, the Spanish banking system can sometimes seem like a confusing labyrinth to newcomers.

This guide simplifies the bureaucracy and explains step by step how to open a bank account in Spain. Ready to get started? 👇

❓ Is it absolutely necessary to open a bank account in Spain?

If you are coming for a short tourist holiday, this is not necessary. You can use the maps from your home country.

However, if you plan to stay in Spain for more than 3 months, a local bank account will make your life much easier and is in some cases even essential.

Who needs a Spanish bank account anyway?

  • 🎓 Erasmus, Master's or PhD students.

  • 📅 Holders of long-term student visas (Type D).

  • 💼 Those who work or are doing an internship in Spain.

  • 🏠 For those who will be signing a long-term lease (landlords usually require a Spanish IBAN).

  • 💰 Those who will receive a scholarship or salary payments.

🏦 Account types: Differences between residents and non-residents

In Spain, the first question you will be asked when visiting a bank is: "Are you a resident or not?" This distinction determines the fees to be paid and the complexity of the process.

1. Non-resident account

You have only recently arrived in the country and have not yet received your Temporary Entry Permit (TIE). In this case, you would open this account.

  • ✅ For whom: People who do not yet have a Physical Entry Permit (TIE).

  • 💸 Disadvantage: Monthly account fees are usually higher, and some banks may require additional bureaucratic effort, such as a "certificate of non-residentship" (certificado de no residencia).

2. Resident account (Located in the "Residents" section)

This is the account type you need to switch to once you have completed your registration process.

  • ✅ For whom: People who have received their NIE number and are in possession of a TIE (residence permit).

  • 💰 Advantage: The costs are much lower (often free for students) and you have access to a wider range of banking services.

💡 Tip: Even if you initially open a non-resident account, don't forget to switch your account to resident status with your bank as soon as you receive your Time Identification Card (TIE). This will help you avoid unnecessary costs.

📝 What documents are required for a bank account?

In Spain, the required documents can vary slightly from bank to bank and even from branch to branch. However, preparing this "golden folder" before your appointment will speed up the process.

  1. Passport: Original copy of your valid passport.

  2. NIE number (if applicable): The foreign identification number that begins with "Y" or "Z" and is printed on your visa.

  3. Registration certificate (Empadronamiento): A document that proves your residence. You may need a rental agreement or a registration certificate (Empadronamiento) from the municipality.

  4. Status document: A document that proves what you intend to do in Spain. (Certificate of enrollment, university admission letter or internship contract).

🏆 Most popular banks in Spain

Here are some of the banks that are frequently used by students and expats and where you are more likely to find English-speaking support:

  • 🔵 BBVA: It has a very strong digital infrastructure, its app is award-winning, and opening an account is relatively easy for new customers.

  • 🔴 Santander: One of Spain's largest banks. It may have agreements with universities.

  • ⭐ CaixaBank: Has a very extensive branch network.

  • 🟠 ING: Generally a more affordable, digitally focused option.

  • ⚪ Sabadell: Another established bank that is widely preferred.

💡 Tip: Be sure to ask about the "student package" (cuenta joven / cuenta estudiante) at the branch. These packages usually offer free accounts and cards for people up to 25-30 years old.

💻 Are online banks (neobanks) an option?

Yes! Fully digital banks (neobanks) like N26 or Revolut can be lifesaving for newcomers to Spain.

  • ✅ Advantage: You receive a European IBAN within minutes – using only your passport and smartphone, without having to visit a branch. Ideal for receiving grant funding or making initial payments.

  • ⚠️ Attention: Some official institutions or older landlords may not accept the IBANs of these banks (especially if they do not offer a Spanish ES IBAN). However, it is a good temporary solution until a main account is opened.

⚠️ The 4 most common mistakes

To avoid unnecessarily prolonging the process and losing money, you should avoid the following mistakes:

  1. Incorrect account type: Opening a standard account with high costs without indicating that you are a student.

  2. No appointment necessary: In Spain, banks generally operate by appointment (cita previa). Don't go too early in the morning, or you'll be turned away.

  3. Submitting incomplete documents: The "I'll bring them later" approach doesn't work in Spanish bureaucracy. Make sure your documents are complete.

Conclusion: Early preparation pays off.

Opening a bank account in Spain isn't rocket science, but it does require patience and the right information. It's especially beneficial for Erasmus students or other newcomers to research the different options beforehand and have the necessary documents ready so they can enjoy their first few weeks in Spain without any worries.

Good luck! 🍀

The first real shock for students coming to France is the high cost of living. Between rent, transportation, groceries, and social life, most students are forced to work sooner rather than later. However, working in France is not like working in Türkiye. The rules are clear, the system is slow, and the consequences of mistakes can be severe.

🎓 What are the rights to work with a student visa?

In France, anyone holding a student visa is legally entitled to work 964 hours per year . This equates to approximately 20 hours per week.

This is the right to work. It applies to university students. It applies to master's and doctoral students. It also applies to language school students.

So the idea that "I can't work because I'm at a language school" is completely wrong. What matters is that your visa type is student status.

Some employers may employ you full-time during public holidays and the summer months. However, the total annual limit should not exceed 964 hours.

💶 Salaries. Are they really enough when you work?

This money alone won't guarantee a comfortable life. But it will prevent you from going hungry. It will cover part of the rent. It will reduce your dependence on your family.

In France, student work is done to survive, not to make ends meet .

🍽️ The Easiest Fields to Find a Job In and the Facts

Those with a low level of French usually start in the following areas: Restaurant kitchen 🍳 Dishwashing and cleaning 🧽 Warehousing and logistics 📦

These jobs are physically demanding, but the onboarding process is quick. They don't require French language skills and are usually found through connections.

For those with an intermediate level of French, the options expand: Waitressing ☕ Cashiering 🛒 Fast food chains 🍔 Hotel jobs 🏨

The easiest jobs for university students are on-campus jobs. Examples include: Library assistant 📚, Student affairs office 🏫, Exam and event organization.

These jobs are both insured and compatible with the curriculum.

s

⚠️ Illegal Employment. Nobody Says It, But the Truth Is Harsh.

Working illegally is very common in France, but that doesn't make it safe. While it may seem to bring in more money in the short term, the cost is high in the long term.

Consequences of working illegally: Risk of refusal to renew residency permit; fines and legal action against the employer; negative track record in future visa applications.

Especially when your prefecture file is being reviewed, insurance records are checked. If it is determined that you were working illegally, a defense of good faith is usually ineffective.

In short, the system in France is slow but has a strong memory.

You've come to Spain for your education; classes have started, the city is wonderful, the tapas are delicious... But the Euro exchange rate is a factor. 📉 Many students and researchers ask this question to ease their tuition costs or earn some pocket money: "Can I study and work at the same time?"

Answer: Yes, but only if you follow the rules.

Working in Spain on a student visa is a complex issue full of grey areas. One wrong step can even lead to your visa being revoked. This guide explains legal working hours, internship (prácticas) processes, and post-graduation opportunities in the clearest way possible.

Ready? Let's open your career file in Spain! 💼👇

🎓 1. Is it possible to work in Spain with a student visa?

Yes, you can work. However, the Spanish government doesn't want you to forget that your priority is "education." Therefore, there are some restrictions.

What are the rules?

  • ⏳ Time Limit: You are allowed to work a maximum of 30 hours per week. (Previously 20 hours, relaxed with new regulations).

  • 📚 Avoiding Conflicts with Education: Your work hours should not conflict with your class hours.

  • 📝 Formal Contract: An employment contract (contrato) is mandatory. Working "without insurance" (en negro) is a crime and carries the risk of deportation.

⚠️ Important Note: A student visa does not automatically grant you the right to work "full-time". While full-time work is permitted during holiday periods, it must be part-time during the academic year.

📄 2. How to Obtain a Work Permit? (The process works in reverse)

The "let me get my permit first, then look for a job" mentality that exists in Türkiye doesn't work here. In Spain, the process works like this:

  1. First, you find an employer who will hire you.

  2. Your employer will apply to the Immigration Office (Extranjería) on your behalf.

  3. "I'm hiring this student part-time, it won't affect their studies," he guarantees.

  4. You can start working if the government approves.

In other words, the company that will hire you submits the application, not you. This bureaucracy may make some employers hesitant to hire students.

💼 3. Internship (Prácticas) Topic: Do I Need Leave of Absence?

Internships are easier to obtain than work permits and involve less bureaucracy. They fall into two categories:

A) Compulsory Internship (Curricular)

If your internship is part of your university curriculum (i.e., you are earning credits):

  • ✅ No additional work permit is required.

  • A tripartite agreement (Convenio) is signed between the university, the company, and the student, and then you begin.

B) Voluntary / Post-Graduation Internship (Extracurricular)

It's not mandatory in the course curriculum, but if you're doing it for experience:

  • An agreement should be made through the university again.

  • The process is more flexible for Erasmus+ trainees, but a grant document and a Learning Agreement are required.

🚀 4. Post-Graduation: Job Seeker Visa (Stay Back Option)

Have you completed your undergraduate or postgraduate studies in Spain and want to stay? We have great news.

You can obtain a "Residence Permit for Job Seeking or Entrepreneurship" (Residencia para la búsqueda de empleo).

  • 📅 Duration: This gives you the right to stay in Spain and look for a job for 12 months .

  • 🎯 Objective: If you find a job in your field or start a company during this period, you can change your status to "Work Permit".

  • ⚠️ Important: You must apply for this permit before your student visa expires (usually 60 days before). Don't miss the deadline!

🔎 5. In Which Fields Do Students Find Jobs Most Easily?

Finding a job without speaking Spanish is difficult, but not impossible. Your chances are particularly high in the following sectors:

  • ☕ Tourism & Services: Waiters/bartenders fluent in English are wanted in locations such as Barcelona and Madrid.

  • 🏫 Language Schools: Offering private lessons in English or Turkish (though rarely).

  • 💻 Start-up & Technology: If you are a software developer or digital marketer, the language barrier is lower.

  • 👶 Au Pair / Babysitting: Childcare provided by a host family.

🛑 6. The Most Common Mistakes and Risks

The following mistakes could end your Spanish adventure prematurely, so be careful:

  1. Working Illegally (Trabajo en Negro): Offers like "Let's not provide insurance, let's pay in cash" may seem appealing, but if caught, you will be deported and will never be able to obtain a Schengen visa again.

  2. Exceeding 30 Hours: Don't attempt to work full-time on a student visa.

  3. Neglecting Classes: When renewing your visa, you will be required to provide a "certificate of academic performance" from your school. If you fail classes while working, your visa will not be renewed.

  4. Working Without NIE/TIE: No one can legally hire you without your residence permit.

💰 7. Banking and Social Security

The moment you start your job, you will need two things:

  1. Spanish Bank Account: For salary payments.

  2. Social Security Number (Número de la Seguridad Social): You receive this once, and it's valid for life. Your employer uses this number when insuring you and includes you in the health system.

Conclusion: It's Possible with the Right Steps

Working while studying in Spain can help save money and speed up your Spanish practice. Just be aware that bureaucracy can be a bit slow, and do everything according to the rules.

Stay tuned to the blog for more tips on career opportunities and life in Spain!

In this article, we're putting aside urban legends and examining current living costs in Spain based on grocery receipts, rental agreements, and real student experiences . Get your pens and paper ready? Let's start budget planning! 👇

🤔 Is student life expensive in Spain?

Short answer: It depends on which city you're in.

Spain is still a more "student-friendly" country compared to northern countries like France or Germany. However, there is almost a twofold cost difference between living in central Madrid and living in Granada.

Now let's look at the average (rent + living) costs by city.

🏙️ Average Monthly Expenses by City

The figures are based on a standard student lifestyle (room in a shared apartment + groceries + transportation + social life).

1. Madrid & Barcelona (Major League) 🚩

These are the two most expensive cities in Spain.

2. Valencia (Golden Center) 🍊

A popular Erasmus city offering both the amenities of a large city and relative affordability.

3. Seville, Granada & Southern Cities (Budget-Friendly) 💃

Andalusia is a paradise for students on a budget.

🏠 The Biggest Cost: Rent and Accommodation

Be prepared to allocate half of your budget to accommodation.

🛒 Kitchen and Social Life: Will I Go Hungry?

Absolutely not! Grocery prices in Spain are reasonable.

🚌 Transportation and Hidden Expenses

Those "small" details often forgotten when budgeting:

  • Youth Cards: Many cities offer significantly discounted transportation cards for those under 26 (Abono Joven). Get one during your first week there.

🎓 The Critical Question: Is the Erasmus Grant Sufficient?

This is the most frequently asked question. The honest answer: Usually no, it's not enough on its own.

💡 Tip: In southern cities (like Granada), there are students who barely make ends meet with grants alone, but in Madrid/Barcelona, this is nearly impossible.

🤑 4 Golden Tactics to Save Money

  1. Second Hand Groups: Download the "Wallapop" app. It's Spain's Letgo. It's great for buying and selling items.

  2. Museums are free: Many museums are free for students or for everyone on Sundays.

  3. Botteón Culture: Like Spanish students do, buying your drink from the market and socializing in parks is much cheaper than sitting in a bar.

Conclusion: Don't be afraid, plan!

Being a student in Spain, with proper budget management, can turn into one of the best memories of your life, not a nightmare. The key is to set expectations correctly and prepare your Excel spreadsheet beforehand instead of saying "I'll sort it out as soon as I arrive."

Remember; an experience worth every Euro you spend awaits you! ✨

The biggest dilemma most frequently discussed in forums by students considering a master's degree in Spain: Is Valencia or Granada better? 🤔

This isn't just a choice of city; it's a strategic decision that will determine your budget, career, and quality of life in Spain.

In this guide, we examine both Spain and Turkey in an SEO-friendly, transparent, and realistic way, covering everything from the student visa process and cost of living to academic quality and job opportunities.

🔍 The "Golden Rule" to Look For Before the City Name: Program Type

Before falling in love with a city, you should decide on the type of diploma you want. In the Spanish education system, this distinction is vital.

1. Master Oficial vs. Título Propio: What's the Difference? ⚠️

The biggest mistake most students make is being fooled by the program's name.

  • ✅ Official Master's Degree: This is a state-approved degree. You have a very high chance of obtaining YÖK (Turkish Higher Education Council) equivalency . It is mandatory if you want to pursue a PhD. It also provides advantages in the job search visa and residence permit processes in Spain after completing your master's degree.

  • ⚠️ Título Propio (Private Diploma): This is a certificate issued by the university itself. It's more practical, but it generally doesn't offer equivalency to the Turkish Higher Education Council (YÖK) or opens doors to doctoral studies.

👉 Expert Advice: If you are aiming for an academic career or want to use your diploma in official institutions in Turkey, your priority should definitely be a Master's Degree (Máster Oficial) .

🌍 2. Don't Fall into the Language Trap: Is the Education Really in English?

Just because the registration page says "English Taught" doesn't necessarily mean the entire process will be in English. When studying for an English-language master's degree in Spain, you should inquire about the following:

  • The language of elective courses (sometimes only Spanish).

  • Do the administrative staff speak English?

  • Teachers' English proficiency.

📌 Valencia vs Granada: Universities in Valencia (UPV, UV) are more committed to English-language curricula due to the high concentration of international students. In Granada, however, Spanish may be more dominant due to the influence of social life and local culture.

🆚 The Big Comparison: Valencia or Granada?

To make your decision easier, we compared the two cities based on the most critical factors.

🏠 Cost of Living and Accommodation 💸

When it comes to the cost of living for students in Spain, Granada always stands out for being budget-friendly.

🏢 Bureaucracy and Student Affairs ⏳

Spanish bureaucracy is notorious, but there are differences in speed between cities.

  • Valencia: The immigration office and universities are very accustomed to international students. Email responses and the TIE (Residence Permit) processes are relatively more systematic.

  • Granada: Academic quality is very high (especially the University of Granada, which has a long history), but bureaucratic processes can sometimes move at a "siesta" pace.

💼 Career and Job Opportunities 🚀

What are your plans after graduation?

  • Valencia: Spain's third largest city. You have a much higher chance of finding internships and jobs in technology, start-ups, logistics, and engineering.

  • Granada: It excels more in academia, research, history, and linguistics. Private sector job opportunities are more limited compared to Valencia.

📝 3. Course Content and Academic Quality (Check-List)

Before applying for a master's degree in Spain, be sure to find the answers to these questions:

  • [ ] Is there a mandatory internship in the curriculum? (It would make finding a job easier).

  • [ ] What is the ECTS (Credit) distribution?

  • [ ] Is it project and lab-based, or theoretical?

  • [ ] Is it possible to choose English as the thesis writing language?

✅ Result: Which City Should You Choose?

There isn't just one "best," there's only what's most suitable for your goal .

  1. Valencia is the right choice for you if:

    • If you want to stay in Spain after graduation and work in the private sector.

    • If you like the amenities of a big city and the sea.

    • If you're looking for a more professional and English-friendly environment.

  2. If Granada is the right choice for you:

    • If you have a limited budget and want to have an economical student life.

    • If you want to experience authentic Spanish culture and student life (Tapas life!).

    • If you are academically focused or your priority is improving your Spanish.

🎯 Don't leave your dream of playing in Spain to chance!

The master's program in Spain is not just about choosing a school; it's a chain of events involving acceptance, visa preparation, residence permit, and accommodation . One incorrect document can lead to lost semesters and financial losses.

While studying at a university in Italy is a dream for many students, the Euro exchange rate and living costs can often be daunting. However, for those targeting universities based in Turin, there is an opportunity to turn this around: the EDISU Piemonte Scholarship.

EDISU, one of Italy's most reliable and advantageous regional scholarships, is a true "game changer" for Turkish students. So, what is this scholarship, who is eligible, and how can you win it? Here's everything you need to know about the financial keys to studying in Italy.

What is the EDISU Piemonte Scholarship?

EDISU Piemonte is the official regional state scholarship system for students studying in the Piedmont region of Italy. This system is based on the "Diritto allo studio" (Right to Education) principle enshrined in the Italian constitution.

The primary goal of this scholarship is not to reward academically gifted individuals, but rather to enable students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds to pursue their education on equal terms. In other words, it's not a merit-based scholarship, but rather an income-based social support system.

What does the EDISU Scholarship offer students?

EDISU Piemonte is one of the systems in Italy that comes closest to the concept of a "full scholarship". A student who wins the scholarship is relieved of four of the biggest expenses in their education:

  • 💰 Annual Cash Scholarship: Cash support deposited into the student's account throughout the academic year, often sufficient to cover basic living expenses.

  • 🏠 Accommodation: Free or very low-cost accommodation in state-run dormitories affiliated with EDISU. Cash rent assistance is also available if a dormitory place is not available. (This is a vital advantage in a city like Turin where rents are high.)

  • 🍽️ Cafeteria Card: Entitles you to eat for free or at a symbolic price in university cafeterias.

  • 📄 Tuition Fee Waiver: University tuition fees are either completely waived or reduced to a minimum level.

Who is eligible to apply for the EDISU Piemonte Scholarship?

A very large percentage of students going from Türkiye to Italy are eligible for this scholarship.

1. University and Regional Requirement

Priority will be given to students who will be studying at state universities, especially in the city of Turin :

  • Politecnico di Torino

  • University of Turin (Unito)

  • Other public universities in the Piedmont region

2. Education Level

  • License (Laurea)

  • Master's Degree (Laurea Magistrale)

  • Doctorate (PhD)

3. Citizenship

The scholarship is offered equally to Turkish students with non-EU status , not just EU citizens.

What does "Income-Oriented System" mean?

This is the most critical aspect of the EDISU Piemonte scholarship. When your application is evaluated, your family's economic situation is considered before your GPA.

The system analyzes the following:

  1. The family's annual income.

  2. Real and movable assets.

  3. Household size and structure.

Important Note: Academic achievement is secondary for this scholarship. A very high GPA is not required; however, it is essential that your documents are accurate, complete, and prepared in accordance with Italian bureaucratic requirements .

Why are EDISU Scholarships Lost? (Most Common Mistakes)

Many students and parents start the process thinking, "Our financial situation allows it, we'll definitely get in," but are eliminated due to technical errors. Although EDISU is one of the most regular paying institutions, it is also one of the most bureaucratic.

Common mistakes include:

  • Income documents were not prepared according to Turkish standards and were not converted to the Italian format (ISEE Parificato).

  • Deficiencies in the translation and apostille processes.

  • Leaving the application until the last minute and system errors.

  • Incorrect calculation of household income.

Who is it ideal for?

If your goal is Politecnico di Torino or other universities in the region, and your family lives in Turkey and you want to focus solely on your education without having to work in Italy, then EDISU Piemonte is the safest option for you.

This scholarship is lost not because it is impossible to win, but because the application was submitted incorrectly .

What is the ESU Venezia Scholarship?

ESU Venezia is the official regional state scholarship system for students pursuing higher education in the Venice Region. Based on the "Diritto allo studio" (Right to Education) principle in the Italian constitution, this system aims for social justice rather than purely academic achievement.

What does the ESU Venezia Scholarship offer students?

ESU Venezia is much more than "partial support". In Venice's challenging economic conditions, it offers students a complete shield of protection:

When it comes to education in Italy, the first thing that comes to mind is the University of Padua (Università di Padova), one of the oldest universities in the world, where Galileo Galilei taught. However, the cost of studying at this prestigious institution may be a concern for Turkish students.

This is where the ESU Padova Scholarship , provided by the Veneto Region, comes into play. This system, which is the second most applied for by international students after EDISU Piemonte, opens the doors to "zero-cost" education in Italy when managed with the right strategy.

What is the ESU Padova Scholarship?

ESU Padova is an official regional state scholarship funded by the Veneto Region of Italy and offered to students of the University of Padova.

The fundamental philosophy of this system is the "Diritto allo studio" (Right to Education) principle in the Italian constitution. This means that this scholarship is awarded not only to academically gifted students, but also to successful students who need economic support . In the application evaluation, the family's economic situation is a determining factor, rather than grade point average.

Scholarship Scope: What Does it Provide to the Student?

  • 💰 Annual Cash Payment: Cash support calculated based on the student's income bracket, paid in installments throughout the academic year. This amount is usually sufficient to cover basic living expenses.

  • 📄 Tuition Fee Waiver: Scholarship students are either completely exempt from university tuition fees or pay a symbolic fee.

  • 🏠 Accommodation Support: Accommodation is available in dormitories affiliated with ESU. If dormitory accommodation is not available, students living in private homes may receive cash payments to cover rent.

  • 🍽️ Cafeteria Card: Allows you to eat for free or at a very low price (discounted) in university cafeterias.

Who can apply?

Students applying from Turkey are considered to be in the non-EU category and are fully eligible for the scholarship.

  • Institution: University of Padua (UniPD) or conservatories/fine arts academies in the region.

  • Level: Undergraduate, Master's, and (in some cases) Doctoral students.

Warning: ESU Padova Does Not Tolerate "Minor Mistakes"!

The biggest difference between ESU Padova and other Italian scholarships (e.g., EDISU Piemonte) is the level of strictness in document control.

Padua is one of the regions with the lowest tolerance when it comes to paperwork.

  • Income Documents: Must strictly adhere to the Italian format.

  • Asset Declaration: Failure to fully declare family assets such as property deeds, vehicles, or bank assets is automatically grounds for rejection, even if there is no malicious intent.

  • Format: The way documents are uploaded to the system, as well as translation and apostille details, are of vital importance.

Crucial Information: The ESU Padova scholarship is earned through discipline , not luck. The "I uploaded the documents, hopefully I'll get it" mentality unfortunately doesn't work in Padova.

Common Mistakes and Reasons for Rejection

Every year, hundreds of students who are actually in a position to qualify for scholarships are rejected due to these simple mistakes:

  1. Incorrect Income Calculation: Incorrect adaptation of income figures in Turkey to the Italian ISEE (Income Indicator) system.

  2. Incomplete Asset Declaration: If an insignificant asset like a "worthless plot of land in the village" or an "old model car" is not declared, the scholarship will be forfeited.

  3. Translation Errors: Deficiencies in sworn translations and consular/apostille certifications.

  4. Incorrect Year Selection: Confusing the desired tax year (usually the two years preceding the application year).

Being a Student in Padua

Padua is a true student city where the cost of living is slightly more balanced compared to Turin or Milan. Transportation is easy, the city is safe, and the academic environment is very strong. A student receiving an ESU scholarship can focus on their studies without having to work a second job.

When planning a university education in Italy, most students look to Milan, Rome, or Turin. However, for those who think "strategically," there is a shining opportunity in the northeast of the Italian map: Trieste.

The ARDiS Scholarship offered by the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region is one of the most accessible opportunities for Turkish students to study in Italy. This region, where competition is more balanced compared to larger cities and living costs are lower, is ideal for a budget-friendly education.

So, what is the ARDiS Trieste scholarship and how can you seize this opportunity? Here are the details.

What is the ARDiS Trieste Scholarship?

ARDiS (Agenzia Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio) is an official regional state scholarship for students studying at higher education institutions in the Friuli-Venezia Giulia region of Italy.

Like EDISU in Turin or ESU in Venice, this system is based on the principle of "Diritto allo studio" (Right to Education). However, the biggest difference with ARDiS is the economic structure of the city of Trieste. Although the scholarship amount is at similar levels to other regions, the lower cost of rent and living in Trieste increases the student's purchasing power.

Scholarship Scope: To be a Student in Trieste

A student who wins the ARDiS scholarship minimizes their tuition costs. The scholarship package includes:

  • 💰 Annual Cash Payment: Cash support paid in installments throughout the year, determined according to the family's income. (In Trieste, this money is much more generous compared to Milan.)

  • 🏠 Dormitory and Accommodation Support: Accommodation is available in student dormitories affiliated with ARDiS. If the dormitory capacity is full or the student chooses to live in a private house, a cash payment to cover rent is provided.

  • 🍽️ Cafeteria Service: Free or discounted meals at university cafeterias (Mensa).

  • 📄 Complete Tuition Fee Exemption: University tuition fees would be completely eliminated or reduced to a symbolic level.

Who is eligible to apply for the ARDiS Scholarship?

Trieste is one of the most advantageous cities for Turkish students with Non-EU (non-EU) status.

  • Institutions: Primarily the University of Trieste (Università degli Studi di Trieste) , as well as conservatories and higher education institutions in the region.

  • Level: Undergraduate, Master's, and Doctoral students.

  • Criteria: Academic achievement is not required for application; the primary criterion is the family's economic situation.

Why Trieste? (Strategic Perspective)

Thousands of students applying for Italian scholarships often concentrate in large cities. This can make it difficult to secure a scholarship or even secure a place in the dormitory waiting list. ARDiS Trieste, however, offers the following advantages:

  1. Less Competition: Application volume is lower compared to Turin or Milan.

  2. Student-Friendly City: Trieste is a safe, compact, and peaceful seaside student city.

Points to Note: "Easy City, Difficult Bureaucracy"

The fact that life in Trieste is easy doesn't mean the scholarship application process is lax. On the contrary, the ARDiS system is quite rigorous in its document verification.

Most Common Reasons for Rejection:

  • Missing Apostille: The apostille seal being forgotten on identity or income documents obtained from Turkey.

  • Erroneous Translation: Sworn translations not being certified by the Italian consulate or translation errors.

  • Asset Concealment: Failure to declare real estate (house, land, vehicle) registered in the family's name. Italian authorities demand transparency in this regard.

  • Formatting Errors: Documents are uploaded to the system in the wrong category or in the wrong format.

Remember: The ARDiS scholarship is not won with a high GPA, but with a well-prepared and timely submitted application .

Conclusion: Who is it ideal for?

If you have a limited budget and prefer to focus your education in a quieter, safer, and more affordable city rather than a crowded and expensive metropolis, then the University of Trieste and the ARDiS scholarship are the most logical combination for you.

The biggest risk in this process is getting bogged down in bureaucratic details.

The biggest question on the minds of students who want to study in Italy is usually: "Which university is better?"

However, for a student or parent with a limited budget, the real (and more strategic) question to ask is: "In which city is it easier and more economical to get a scholarship?"

In this guide, we compared Italy's most important scholarship systems based on "availability" and "cost of living".

🧭 Our Comparison Criteria

We based this analysis on the following four key factors:

  1. Total Scholarship Benefit: The combined value of cash + accommodation + meal support.

  2. Possibility of Getting a Dormitory Room: A chance to avoid accommodation costs.

  3. Level of Competition: Number of student applications and acceptance rate.

  4. Cost of Living in the City: The purchasing power of the scholarship in that city.

🥇 1. Torino (EDISU Piemonte): "Golden Ratio"

Turin is by far the safest destination for a Turkish student wishing to study in Italy.

  • Why? The EDISU system is very well-established and well-organized. Competition is more manageable compared to Milan.

  • The advantage: Rents in Turin are almost half that of Milan. Despite this, the scholarship amount is similar. Furthermore, EDISU has ample dormitory capacity.

  • The result: You get your scholarship, you get a dorm room (or find suitable housing), and you get to enjoy student life.

🥈 2. Trieste (ARDiS): "Hidden Treasure"

If you're someone who says , "For me, it's not the name of the university that matters, but studying without having to pay anything out of pocket," then Trieste should be your destination.

  • Why? It's away from the chaos and competition of big cities. Non-EU students have a much higher chance of receiving scholarships.

  • The advantage: Trieste is an inexpensive city. The cash scholarship you receive here can allow you to live like a "wealthy" student.

  • Result: Minimum stress, maximum economic comfort.

🥉 3. Padua and Venice (ESU): "A Power That Demands Attention"

Venice and Padua are cities with very high quality education but extremely fragile bureaucracy.

  • Why? The ESU system is unforgiving of even the slightest error in documentation and revenue calculations (ISEE).

  • The advantage: In a touristy and expensive city like Venice, an ESU scholarship (especially if you get a dorm room) is a lifesaver.

  • Conclusion: A flawless application provides a huge advantage; however, amateur applications often end in disappointment.

⚠️ 4. Milan (DSU): "High Risk, High Return"

Everyone dreams of going to Milan... But the DSU Milan scholarship is a real "den of wolves".

  • Why? The number of applications is in the tens of thousands. The chances of getting a dorm room (for the first year) are quite low.

  • Conclusion: Go for it if your file is very strong and you're willing to face competition. Otherwise, Torino might be a more sensible option.

❌ The Most Common Mistake: The "A scholarship is a scholarship" Mentality

The biggest misconception among students and parents is: "Our income is low, we can get scholarships from everywhere."

This is wrong.

With the same income documents and the same family situation;

  • They might not be able to get a dorm room in Milan because of their ranking.

  • You might be disqualified in Padova because of document format issues.

Therefore, when choosing a university, you should consider not only academic goals but also the compatibility between the city and scholarship opportunities .

🎯 Which City is the Right Place for You?

The answer to this question doesn't depend on a single variable. Your family's income, your target major, your risk tolerance, and your need for accommodation should all be considered as a whole.

Don't risk your educational dreams with the wrong city choice or a flawed application strategy. Get professional help to find the best city and scholarship match for your personal circumstances.

Milan... Italy's economic engine, the heart of fashion, and home to world-class universities like Politecnico di Milano , Milano-Bicocca , and Università degli Studi di Milano (Statale) . But this prestige comes at a price: the highest cost of living in Italy.

So, is it possible to avoid being overwhelmed by these high costs while studying at a state university in Milan? The answer: The DSU Milan Scholarship.

This financial support provided by the Lombardy Region is the strongest key to opening the doors of Milan for Turkish students. Here's everything you need to know about this challenging but highly rewarding scholarship system.

What is the DSU Milano Scholarship?

DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) is an official regional state scholarship offered to students studying at public universities in the Lombardy Region.

The logic behind this scholarship is the same as in other Italian regions: "The Right to Education." This means the system targets not the student with the highest academic grades, but the student who most needs financial support and wants to continue their education .

Scholarship Scope: What Does it Provide for Students in Milan?

DSU Milano is more than just pocket money. In a city like Milan, where rent and living costs are expensive, it offers students a complete "survival package":

  • 💰 Annual Cash Grant: Cash support calculated according to family income bracket and paid in installments throughout the year. (Vital for balancing living expenses in Milan.)

  • 🏠 Accommodation Support: Opportunity to stay in DSU-affiliated dormitories.

    • Important Note: Dormitory places in Milan are limited. If a dormitory place is not available, the cash scholarship amount will be increased under the name of "rent assistance". This is a critical support for students who will be renting an apartment in Milan.

  • 🍽️ Cafeteria Service: Daily free or very low-cost meal entitlement at university cafeterias (Mensa).

Who can apply for a DSU Scholarship?

Students applying from Turkey are considered to be in the non-EU category and are fully eligible for the scholarship.

  • Universities:

    • Politecnico di Milano

    • University of Milan (Statale)

    • University of Milano-Bicocca

    • Other public universities and conservatories in the Lombardy region.

  • Level: Bachelor's, Master's, and Doctorate.

Critical Warning: Milan Does Not Tolerate Mistakes!

DSU Milano's scholarship program is the most popular and therefore the most competitive in Italy.

Due to the large number of applications, the evaluation committee (CAF offices and universities) is extremely strict in its document control.

Most Common Reasons for Rejection:

  1. Incorrect Income Declaration: Incorrectly adapting Turkish income to the Italian ISEE Parificato system. (For example, gross/net distinction, pension calculations).

  2. Asset Concealment: Failure to declare assets such as "old model cars" or "shared ownership of land." If non-compliance with the Italian tax system is detected, the scholarship will be immediately terminated.

  3. Document Format: Lack of apostille, incorrect translation, or documents uploaded to the system in the wrong format.

  4. Date Errors: Mixing up the reference year requested in the application.

Remember: In Milan, there's no such thing as a "minor flaw." Your documents are either perfect or rejected.

Living in Milan with a Scholarship

Milan is an expensive city, but a student with a DSU scholarship can complete their education with minimal burden on their family thanks to a cafeteria pass, tuition waiver, and cash support. While navigating Milan without a scholarship can be challenging, with DSU, it becomes a rewarding experience.

🎯 Don't risk your Milan dream!

Getting accepted to schools like Politecnico di Milano or Unimi is difficult; however, winning and retaining a scholarship requires the right strategy.

In this system with thousands of competitors, your application needs to be error-free. Get professional support for income calculation (ISEE), document collection, translation and apostille processes, and application tracking.

“Which Italian city gives me the best chance of a scholarship?” is a useful starting question, but a city ranking cannot answer it reliably. A successful application depends on the applicable call, your household circumstances, academic record, enrolment status and supporting documents. There is no verified basis here for calling Turin or Trieste a near-guaranteed choice, or for assigning star ratings to a student's chances.

Italy's regional right-to-study support can combine cash, meals, fee relief and accommodation. The institution responsible for a scholarship is not always the organisation managing residences. Compare the rules for the university and campus you will actually attend, rather than assuming that every student in a city enters a single scholarship pool.

Turin: start with EDISU Piemonte

EDISU Piemonte awards scholarships through an annual public call, subject to financial and academic requirements and available funding. International applicants must also check the specific documentation procedure.

Turin may suit your academic plans, but satisfying an income threshold alone does not prove that you will receive money or a room. Read the definitions of eligible applicant, beneficiary and residence allocation. Keep separate records of the scholarship application and any accommodation request. Compare the timing of results with the date on which a landlord requires a deposit.

Trieste: read the ARDiS unified call

ARDiS Friuli Venezia Giulia publishes a unified call covering scholarships, accommodation and other benefits for the institutions within its remit. Each benefit has its own conditions and timetable.

A smaller city does not by itself establish lower competition or a higher success rate. Check whether your programme is covered, how foreign household finances must be certified, and how a room offer must be accepted. Consider a second housing option while awaiting results. An eligible scholarship application should not be treated as confirmed accommodation.

Padua: distinguish scholarship and housing procedures

The University of Padua publishes the regional scholarship call and application instructions, including financial certification and enrolment steps. Read the university procedure alongside the relevant accommodation information.

Assess financial discrepancies under the rules of the relevant call. The published rules, the kind of discrepancy and any available correction or review procedure govern the outcome. Check all figures carefully, but ask the responsible office how to correct an error rather than assuming that every problem has the same consequence.

Venice: check your university's call and ESU services

Ca' Foscari manages regional scholarship awards on behalf of Veneto; ESU Venezia manages accommodation and canteen services described in that system. Other institutions require their own checks.

For a student considering Ca' Foscari or IUAV, the practical question is the total budget after the actual support offered. Compare the teaching location, travel costs, lease duration and deposit. Check whether off-site status requires a qualifying paid rental contract. Do not assume that a scholarship automatically includes a residence place or covers every housing expense.

Milan: identify the university, not a single “DSU Milano”

Politecnico di Milano publishes its own DSU call. Its benefits can include cash and services, while reduced-rate accommodation requires an application under the applicable rules.

Use the relevant university's call for your own case; Polimi's procedure cannot stand in for Statale or Bocconi. There is no support here for declaring all Milan applicants part of one pool or for estimating a first-year residence success rate. Assess a private-room budget as a contingency, and check the university's formal results before relying on an award.

Università Cattolica: read EDUCatt separately

EDUCatt runs an annual income-and-merit scholarship competition for eligible Cattolica students. Its call defines the benefits and the procedure through MyEDUCatt.

A scholarship, a fee reduction and admission to a residence can have different conditions. Compare their combined effect on your own fees and living costs; neither the word “private” nor the name of the provider tells you what your final contribution will be.

Comparison checklist

City / institutionWhere to startWhat to verify
TurinEDISU PiemonteFinancial/academic requirements; scholarship and room outcomes
TriesteARDiS unified callCovered institutions; separate deadlines and benefit conditions
PaduaUniversity regional scholarship callCertification, enrolment and housing procedure
Venice / Ca’ FoscariUniversity call; ESU Venezia servicesAward procedure and accommodation allocation
Milan / PolimiUniversity DSU callRelevant university, cash/services and housing request

How to make a decision without invented probabilities

  1. Choose academically suitable programmes first, then obtain the correct call for each university, campus and academic year.

  2. Check household income and assets, the certification required for foreign finances, previous study and academic progress rules. Record which requirements apply now and which must be met later to retain the benefit.

  3. Make a calendar for the application, document submission, provisional ranking, review request, final outcome and acceptance of any housing offer. Save receipts and official messages.

  4. Prepare two budgets: one based only on funds already available, and another including an award after it is confirmed. Include deposits, travel and the period before any payment arrives.

  5. If a rule is unclear, send the relevant office a precise question with the call article and your applicant category. Do not pay anyone who promises a guaranteed scholarship.

The sensible choice is the programme and funding arrangement whose requirements you can meet and whose financial gap you can manage. Deadlines, amounts and documents change by academic year: the linked calls and official updates take priority over this general comparison.

Studielink Guide. How to Apply to Universities in the Netherlands Step by Step (2026)

Studying at a university in the Netherlands means earning one of Europe’s most prestigious diplomas. However, the Dutch application system is slightly different from the familiar “one click application” model. The process is two-step and operates under quota-based rules (Numerus Fixus).

If you are planning to study in the Netherlands for the 2026 academic year, you must understand the Studielink system and its rules in advance. Registering on Studielink alone does not mean your application is complete. Many students realize this too late.

Below is a comprehensive Studielink guide and strategic tips that form the foundation of Dutch university applications.

What Is Studielink?

Studielink is the official government-run central registration platform used to apply to all higher education institutions in the Netherlands, including Research Universities and Universities of Applied Sciences.

It can be compared to the ÖSYM system in Turkey. However, instead of exam scores, Studielink processes application intent and personal data. Creating a Studielink registration is the first and mandatory step in applying to any Dutch university.

Why Is the Dutch Application System Two-Step?

The most common mistake is assuming that the process ends with Studielink. In reality, that is where it begins.

Step 1. Studielink Registration (Opening the Door)You enter your personal information and create an “enrolment application” stating that you wish to apply to a specific program at a specific university. At this stage, no documents are uploaded.

Step 2. University Portal (Submitting the File)Within 24–48 hours after completing your Studielink registration, you receive an email from the university containing login details for its own application portal (for example Osiris or MyUnimaas).

This is where the real application happens.

You upload:

  • Diploma and transcript

  • Motivation letter and CV

  • Language certificate (IELTS/TOEFL)

  • Reference letters if required

Your application will not be evaluated until the university portal is fully completed.

Application Limits and the Numerus Fixus Rule

Studielink does not allow unlimited applications. Strategy matters.

Total Program Limit. 4You may apply to a maximum of 4 programs per academic year. These can be distributed across different universities.

What Is Numerus Fixus? The Most Critical Rule

Numerus Fixus refers to programs with limited capacity that select students through a competitive selection process rather than grades alone. Popular programs such as Psychology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and International Business often fall into this category.

⚠️ The rule is clear.Out of your 4 total applications, a maximum of 2 can be Numerus Fixus programs.

Example. 2 Numerus Fixus + 2 regular programs is allowed.Mistake. Applying to 3 Numerus Fixus programs is not possible. The system will block it.

Critical Dates for 2026 Applications

The Dutch application calendar is strict. Missing a deadline can cost you an entire year.

  • 15 January 2026 (Very Important). Final deadline for Numerus Fixus programs. No exceptions.

  • 1 April / 1 May 2026. General deadlines for regular programs.

Advisor’s Note.Non-EU students, including Turkish applicants, should complete applications by February–March to allow time for visa and accommodation procedures. May can be too late.

Step-by-Step Application Strategy

A correct Dutch application follows these steps:

  • Program selection. Identify which programs are Numerus Fixus.

  • Studielink account. Create your account using passport details.

  • Start enrolment. Enter up to 4 choices.

  • Email tracking. Monitor portal invitation emails, including spam folders.

  • Document upload. Complete the university portal with all required documents.

  • Selection process. Prepare for exams or interviews if applying to Numerus Fixus programs.

Most Common Mistakes

  • Relying only on Studielink and ignoring the university portal.

  • Missing the 15 January Numerus Fixus deadline.

  • Delaying accommodation search. Housing in the Netherlands is often harder than gaining admission.

🎯 No Room for Risk in Your Dutch Dream

How should you distribute your 4 application choices? Which universities fit your profile best? How should you prepare for Numerus Fixus selection exams?

Dutch university applications require strategic planning. Do not leave your 2026 application to chance.

A Complete Guide for Bachelor, Master and Numerus Fixus Programs

One of the biggest mistakes in Dutch university applications is assuming that the process is just about “uploading documents.” In reality, the dynamics of a Bachelor application to the University of Amsterdam and a Master’s application to Delft University of Technology are completely different.

The most common scenario we encounter is this. Documents prepared for Bachelor applications are assumed to be sufficient for Master or Numerus Fixus programs. The result? Automatic rejection emails due to incomplete or incorrect files.

In this guide, we list in detail the documents you must upload to university portals after your Studielink registration, categorized by program type (Bachelor, Master, Numerus Fixus). Always check this list before preparing your application file.

🎓 1. Bachelor (Undergraduate) Application Document Checklist

Bachelor applications are generally simpler. However, the key issue here is diploma equivalency. Dutch universities strictly assess whether your high school diploma is equivalent to the Dutch VWO diploma.

Mandatory Documents

  • High School Diploma or Temporary Graduation Certificate

  • Official Transcript (Grades 9–12, translated into English)

  • Passport or ID copy

  • CV in a simple European format (Europass or similar)

Language Proficiency

  • IELTS / TOEFL meeting the minimum score (usually IELTS 6.0–6.5)

  • Note. Some universities may grant exemptions for IB, AP or fully English-taught high schools.

📌 Advisor’s NoteDiploma equivalency is critical. A Turkish high school diploma may not be sufficient for some research universities (WO), requiring a Foundation year.

🎓🎓 2. Master (Graduate) Application Document Checklist

A Master’s application is not paperwork. It is an academic presentation. Admissions committees closely examine how well your academic background aligns with the chosen program.

Academic and Mandatory Documents

  • Bachelor’s Diploma

  • Bachelor’s Transcript

  • Course Descriptions (critical document explaining course content and syllabi)

  • Passport

Supporting Documents

  • Motivation Letter (Statement of Purpose)

  • Academic CV

  • Reference Letters (usually 2 academic references)

Additional Exams (Program-Based)

  • GMAT / GRE for competitive fields such as Business, Economics or Data Science

🧪 3. Numerus Fixus (Limited Enrollment) Programs

Numerus Fixus programs (Medicine, Psychology, AI, etc.) represent the most competitive track. Uploading documents alone is not enough. You must pass an active selection process.

Basic Documents

  • Passport

  • Language Certificate (must be uploaded before the deadline)

Selection Process Requirements

  • Special Assignments

  • Online cognitive tests (logic, math, subject-based)

  • Motivation questionnaires or structured interviews

⚠️ Critical WarningFor Numerus Fixus programs, 15 January is a strict deadline. Submitting assignments even one hour late results in rejection.

🎯 Final Note

Dutch universities do not select the smartest students. They select the best-prepared application files.

The magical three letters every student hears when preparing for Erasmus: ESN. But what exactly is the Erasmus Student Network, and how can it shape a student’s life abroad so deeply? ESN is not just a student club that organizes parties. It is a massive support network that guides you from the moment you arrive in your new city, helps you socialize, and offers hundreds of discounts.

Here we explore everything ESN provides. from A to Z. enriched with student experiences and practical tips.

💳 ESNcard & Discounts: Your Best Erasmus Wallet Companion

Most Popular ESNcard Discounts:

Transportation

• FlixBus. Offers 10–15% discount on bus travel across Europe. ideal for weekend trips.• Ryanair. Periodic campaigns such as free 20 kg luggage and 10% flight discounts. extremely useful for going home or planning holidays.

Accommodation

• Discounts of 10–20% at major hostel chains like Hostelling International and Generator Hostels.

Food & Drinks

Local ESN partnerships often include bars. cafés and restaurants with 10–30% discounts, making social life more affordable.

Culture & Arts

• Reduced entry for museums. galleries. theaters and cinemas in many cities.

Online Services & Apps

• Language learning. Discounts on Busuu, Babbel, Lingoda.• Music & entertainment. Occasional deals with services like Spotify Student.• Tech & subscriptions. Discounts on platforms like The Economist or certain software tools.

🎉 Social Events: The Heart & Soul of Erasmus

ESN is the main creator of the most unforgettable Erasmus memories. These events help hundreds of students from different countries connect effortlessly.

Popular ESN Events:

• Welcome Week / Welcome Party. The best way to make friends right away.• International Dinner / Global Village. Students bring food from their home countries for a cultural feast.• Pub Crawl. Guided tour of the best student-friendly bars in the city.• Thematic Parties. Halloween, Christmas, St. Patrick’s Day and more.• Tandem & Language Exchange Nights. Practice languages in a fun, relaxed environment.

🚍 Trips: Take Your Erasmus Adventure Beyond Your Host City

ESN organizes affordable and highly social trips so students can explore Europe safely and easily.

Types of ESN Trips:

• Day Trips. Short excursions to nearby cities (e.g., Pisa, Siena, Kutná Hora, Bratislava).• Weekend Trips. Overnight or 2–3 day trips to major destinations (Budapest, Berlin, Cinque Terre, Naples).• National Trips. Large-scale events where ESN sections from the entire country join (e.g., ESN Spain’s Ibiza trip or ESN Italy’s Evento Nazionale).

📌 Student Experience:"The ESN trip to Budapest was the best memory of my Erasmus. If I had gone alone, it would’ve cost more and I wouldn’t have met anyone. The bus trip turned into lifelong friendships." — Elif, Hungary Erasmus Student

📚 Cultural & Academic Support: More Than Just Parties

ESN helps with the administrative and academic challenges of moving abroad.

Examples:

• How-To Sessions: Residence permits, visas, transportation cards, housing.• Workshops & Seminars: CV building, LinkedIn optimization, Erasmus+ internships, volunteering opportunities.• Buddy Program: Local students support you during your first weeks and help you adapt quickly.

👥 ESN Community: Meet Your Erasmus Family

ESN helps you integrate into your new environment quickly.

• Overcoming Culture Shock. Being part of a community reduces loneliness and stress.• International Networking. Meet students from 20–30 different countries in one evening.• Fast Adaptation. Find out where to shop, how to use public transport, and where to eat cheaply.

✅ Conclusion: How ESN Enhances Your Erasmus Experience

Advantages (+):

• Instant social life• Affordable travel• Huge discounts with ESNcard• Guidance for bureaucracy & adaptation• Strong international community

Disadvantages (–):

• Some sections may focus heavily on parties• Trip spots fill up extremely fast• Fewer discounts in small cities

Application requirements and current sources

The Czech official study-residence procedure publishes a 60-day processing limit. The clock does not run during a lawful suspension; this is not a guarantee of a decision within 60 calendar days. Application routes, document requirements and registration deadlines differ between a long-term visa, a residence permit and a D/VR entry visa. Keep proof of submission and comply with any written request for additional documents. A universal 30-day grace period must not be assumed.

Official source · ipc.gov.cz

how-to-fill-out-the-long-term-visa-application-form.pdf

A Czech long-term student visa is an official residence permit issued to students who will participate in an educational program lasting longer than 90 days. Universities. master’s programs. PhD studies. foundation or preparatory courses. language schools. and accredited training programs fall under this category.

With this visa you can.• Legally reside in the country.• Study.• Enroll in your institution.• Complete all official administrative procedures.

The purpose of the visa and all details in the form are determined by the Czech Ministry of the Interior, and the application must be filled out completely and accurately.

📑 2. How to Fill Out the Long-Term Visa Application Form

The application form consists of five pages and must be completed in Latin alphabet block letters. Some fields must be written in Czech. Dates follow the European format, and all information must match the passport exactly.

Below is a page by page explanation.

⭐ Page 1. Personal Information

This page contains basic identity details.

■ 1. Surname

Write it exactly as in the passport, without Turkish characters.

■ 2. Previous surnames

Used only if your surname changed due to marriage. divorce. adoption. If not applicable, leave blank.

■ 3. Given name

Must match your passport.

■ 4. Date of birth

DDMMYYYY format, for example 14032000.

■ 5. Place of birth. region. country code

Country code is three letters. For Turkey. TUR. City name may be written in English.

■ 6. Birth nationality

Usually TUR.

■ 7. Current nationality

For Turkish citizens. TUR.

■ 8. Sex

Male or Female.

■ 9. Marital status

Unmarried. Married. Divorced.

This page is crucial for identity verification, so no spelling mistakes are allowed.

⭐ Page 2. Passport Information and Education

■ 10. Father’s name■ 11. Mother’s name

■ 12. Passport type

Ordinary Passport for regular Turkish passports.

■ 13. Passport number■ 14. Passport issuing country code. TUR■ 15. Date of issue■ 16. Date of expiry

The passport must be valid at least three months beyond the visa end date.

■ 17. Residence permit outside your home country

If you live in Türkiye. leave blank.

■ 18. Occupation

If you are a student. write STUDENT.

■ 19. Current school or employer■ 20. Czech institution where you will study■ 21. Foreign residence address (if applicable)

■ 22. Previous stays in Czechia

If you stayed longer than 3 months previously. list dates and addresses.

■ 23. Address where you will stay in Czechia

Must match your dormitory contract or rental agreement.

■ 24. Postal address, if different■ 25. Requested length of stay. usually 365 DAYS■ 26. Previous Czech visas■ 27. Previous Schengen entries

This page is especially important for accommodation and travel history verification.

⭐ Page 3. Travel Plan and Financial Details

■ 28. Purpose of stay

Studium. Study.

■ 29. Planned arrival date

Can match your dormitory check in date.

■ 30. Planned departure date

Can be left blank if uncertain.

■ 31. Border crossing point

For air travel. PRAHA LETIŠTĚ VÁCLAVA HAVLA.

■ 32. Means of transport

Letadlo, meaning airplane.

■ 33. Inviting person

Leave blank for student applications.

■ 34. Person covering expenses

If you cover costs yourself. select Myself.

■ 35. Type of financial resources

If you submit a bank statement. tick the corresponding boxes. If the account is not in your name. you must provide a notarized and Czech translated authorization letter from your sponsor.

⭐ Pages 4 and 5. Family Information and Contact Details

These sections ask for spouse and children information. If unmarried or without children. leave blank.

■ 38. Home address in Türkiye■ 39. Phone number■ 40. Email address

Finally, you must sign the form and write the location and date of submission.

📌 3. Required Documents for the Czech Student Visa

The visa process is not limited to the form. These documents must be prepared completely.

🔹 Basic document list

• Passport and photocopy• Completed application form• Acceptance letter• Accommodation confirmation• Biometric photo• Bank statements• Additional income documents if applicable• Criminal record certificate with apostille• Birth certificate if required with apostille• Czech official translations of all documents• Health insurance (purchased only after visa approval)

🚀 4. Application Process. Step by Step

✔ 1. Prepare your documents✔ 2. Book an appointment at the consulate✔ 3. Attend the interviewCommon questions.• Why do you want to study in Czechia.• Where will you stay.• How will you fund your stay.

✔ 4. Processing period

Usually 60 days. sometimes up to 90.

✔ 5. Visa approval

You will receive a notification and then purchase health insurance.

🧭 5. Common Mistakes and Important Notes

• Using Turkish characters in the form• Not writing addresses in Czech• Incomplete financial documents• Applying without accommodation• Passport validity too short
