7f64c5c1-71fa-43d4-8b01-3a57a22c4527.title: What to Do if You Receive an Italy Visa Refusal. Explanation of Article 10
7f64c5c1-71fa-43d4-8b01-3a57a22c4527.excerpt: What to Do if You Receive an Italy Visa Refusal. Explanation of Article 10 — Receiving an Article 10 refusal is one of the most common outcomes in Italy national visa applications. Many
7f64c5c1-71fa-43d4-8b01-3a57a22c4527.html:
Receiving an Article 10 refusal is one of the most common outcomes in Italy national visa applications. Many applicants believe they prepared all documents correctly, yet still receive a refusal stating “your travel purpose has not been sufficiently verified” or “the documents provided do not support your stated purpose of travel”. This can be discouraging. however, if you understand the logic behind Article 10 and follow the right steps, you can both identify the real cause and successfully appeal the decision.

In this guide.✔ the real meaning of Article 10.✔ how the consulate evaluates your file.✔ the exact steps to take after a refusal.✔ how to write an effective appeal letter.✔ the most common mistakes and how to fix them. All explained clearly.

🟥 1. What Is Article 10. What Does the Official Explanation Mean

Article 10 is a refusal ground in Italy’s national visa assessment procedure and is usually presented with the following statements.

“Your purpose of travel could not be sufficiently verified.” or “The documents submitted do not support your travel purpose.”

This does not necessarily mean that your documents were missing. it often means that the documents were found inconsistent with each other.

✔ Based on the consulate’s interpretation, Article 10 is issued when.

The travel purpose is not clearly supported by documents.

Bank account activity appears inconsistent.

The accommodation document seems unreliable.

The acceptance letter cannot be verified.

The sponsor’s income is considered insufficient.

Documents appear to be prepared at the last minute.

Previous visa history is considered risky.

The educational purpose is not convincing.

🟥 2. Who Receives Article 10 Refusals Most Often

🔹 Students

Especially in master’s or language school applications.

🔹 Applicants using a sponsor

When the financial connection is not clearly documented.

🔹 Applicants depositing large amounts at once

Irregular bank activity is heavily scrutinized.

🔹 Applicants presenting last minute accommodation

For example, a one-day booking confirmation.

🔹 Applicants whose acceptance letters cannot be verified

Some institutions’ letters raise doubts at the consulate.

🟥 3. What To Do After Receiving a Visa Refusal

There are three possible paths after an Article 10 refusal.

✔ 1. File an Appeal (Ricorso)

This is the strongest method.

📌 Time limit: 30 days

You must submit the appeal within 30 days of receiving the refusal.

📌 Where to file

The appeal is submitted to the Regional Administrative Court of Lazio (TAR Lazio Roma) in Italy.

📌 How it is done.

Through an attorney.

By submitting documents online.

By logically disproving the refusal reason.

The success rate is above 60 percent. especially for Article 10 refusals.

✔ 2. Submit a new application

If you do not want to appeal, you may fix the issues that caused the refusal and reapply.

The new application becomes stronger if.

You correct your bank statement.

You strengthen the sponsor’s financial documents.

You fully resolve any missing document issues.

You ensure verification of your acceptance letter.

It is critical not to repeat the same mistakes.

✔ 3. Wait before reapplying

Some applicants choose to wait 1–2 months to strengthen their bank account activity. This is effective when the refusal was based on weak financial history.

🟥 4. Documents You Should Gather After a Refusal

📌 1. The refusal letter

This is the foundation of your analysis.

📌 2. Updated bank statement

It must show regular inflow and outflow.

📌 3. Updated sponsor income documents

Payroll, social security records, tax documents.

📌 4. Reliable accommodation proof

Long-term, verifiable accommodation is essential.

📌 5. Documents proving your travel purpose.

Acceptance letter.

Detailed academic program.

Course list.

Internship contract.

🟥 5. How To Write an Effective Appeal Letter for Article 10

Below is the logic used by professional attorneys.

📌 Appeal letter logic.

Explain why the consulate’s conclusion is incorrect.

Demonstrate why your purpose of travel is legitimate.

Support your explanation with additional documents.

Attach improved financial evidence.

Use respectful and formal language.

✔ Example introduction paragraph

“Dear Sir or Madam. I believe that the Article 10 refusal issued regarding my application does not reflect the actual circumstances. The documents supporting my educational purpose are complete. and I clearly demonstrate my financial capability through the newly added documentation.”

I can prepare the full appeal letter tailored to your case if you wish.

🟥 6. Golden Tips To Avoid an Article 10 Refusal

✔ Do not deposit money into your account at the last minute.

✔ Show long-term, reliable accommodation.

✔ Prove your relationship with the sponsor through official documents.

✔ Ensure your acceptance letter can be verified by the school.

✔ Include copies of previous visas if applicable.

✔ Add a strong motivation letter explaining your educational purpose.

⭐ Conclusion

Article 10 refusals surprise many applicants. and although the refusal may seem to indicate “insufficient documents”. the actual issue is usually that the documents do not support each other convincingly. With proper analysis, strong documentation, and clear explanations, this refusal ground can be successfully overcome.

0fae8c79-cb84-4e55-a9f3-8fb8cab38b98.title: iDATA Italy Visa Appointments: Official Steps and Student Preparation
0fae8c79-cb84-4e55-a9f3-8fb8cab38b98.excerpt: iDATA Italy Visa Appointments: Official Steps and Student Preparation — Finding an appointment for an Italian visa can take time. Start with the right application category and the current
0fae8c79-cb84-4e55-a9f3-8fb8cab38b98.html:
Finding an appointment for an Italian visa can take time. Start with the right application category and the current instructions of the competent authority. This guide explains official booking channels and practical preparation for students. Receiving an appointment does not mean a visa will be issued: the consulate assesses the application and makes the decision.

1. Identify the correct visa and consular district

Use the actual purpose and length of your stay. A short visit and a long university course require different categories. Do not change a genuine study application into a tourist application merely because an earlier slot appears. An unsuitable category can create problems with the appointment and the documents accepted.

Select an application centre according to the rules of the Italian mission responsible for your place of residence. The Italian Consulate General in Istanbul states that applications must be submitted in the district where the applicant resides. A vacant appointment in another city does not establish eligibility to apply there. If you have moved or have a different legal residence situation, confirm jurisdiction through the official channel first.

2. Begin with the current iDATA Italy website

Open the official iDATA Italy page and read the registration, appointment and document instructions for your category. Enter personal details exactly as shown in your passport. Use an email account you control, complete any verification requested by the system and check the spam folder. Keep application references, payment receipts and appointment confirmations securely.

Do not assume that a telephone number or an old blog link remains the correct channel. Recheck contact details on iDATA and the competent consulate's website before using them. Read applicable fees and cancellation or amendment conditions before completing a transaction. Treat a booking as confirmed only when the official system provides confirmation.

3. Istanbul's special notice for 2026/2027 university enrolment

The Istanbul Consulate's notice of 6 August 2026 says that students whose Universitaly pre-enrolment has been properly approved by the university and transmitted to the Consulate will receive an email from iDATA explaining how to obtain a “Study – University Enrolment” visa appointment. The email address declared in Universitaly is used. If you are waiting for this message, check that the university approval is complete and that your email address is correct.

The same notice gives 30 November 2026 as the deadline for obtaining appointments for the 2026/2027 academic year. Programmes not requiring Universitaly registration, including language courses, exchanges, mobility and other specified programmes, follow the separately described booking process. These dates and procedures concern Istanbul's stated academic year and categories; do not automatically apply them to other missions or future years.

4. What to do when no appointment is displayed

A “no available dates” message does not reveal a secret release hour or priority formula. Follow official announcements. For a technical error, record the message, date and relevant category and contact official support without exposing unnecessary personal data. Automated calling, incessant refreshing and sharing account passwords with strangers are unreliable responses. There is no verified official basis for claiming that repeated calls move an applicant to the front or produce a particular success rate.

If your course is approaching, ask the university in writing about late arrival or enrolment options. Request exceptional or urgent handling only under conditions published by the competent authority. A university letter does not guarantee appointment priority or a visa. Consider the financial implications before buying non-refundable travel on the assumption that an unconfirmed appointment will become available.

5. A practical pre-appointment check

  • Verify passport details, visa category, residential jurisdiction and email address.
  • Read the current document list, including translation, certification and original/copy requirements.
  • Check the location, date and official confirmation; use the official system to cancel or amend.
  • Keep your application tracking reference and answer additional-document requests within the stated period.

Early preparation reduces avoidable errors. It cannot guarantee booking capacity or the visa decision. Recheck official instructions before submitting your application.

  • Italian Consulate General in Istanbul — 2026/2027 university study visa appointments, 6 August 2026

For long-term Erasmus visa applications for Czechia, one of the most common areas where students make mistakes is the criminal record document, apostille, and translation procedures.Students repeatedly ask the same questions.“Should the criminal record be obtained in Czech, is translation required, what happens if the apostille staple comes off, is a notary necessary, which format is accepted?”

This guide was prepared to eliminate all confusion and provide a clear and straightforward explanation.

1️⃣ The Criminal Record Document Can Be Obtained in Czech. No Translation Required

The Czech Consulate accepts the criminal record certificate directly in Czech.In this case, no translation is required.

✔ The most accurate method.

• e-Devlet → Adli Sicil• Download PDF• Print the document

It is fast, free, and requires no translation cost.

2️⃣ If You Obtain the Document in Turkish. Translation Becomes Mandatory. Sworn Translation Required

If the criminal record document is obtained in Turkish, the following may be required.

• Sworn translation• Notary approval• Apostille

For this reason, obtaining it in Czech is the most practical and fastest option.

3️⃣ Apostille Procedure – The Most Critical Rule. NEVER Remove the Staple

The apostille ensures the international validity of your document.The biggest mistake students make is removing the staple when photocopying the document.

✔ If the staple is removed.

• The document becomes invalid• The consulate may reject the visa if they notice it• You must obtain the document again

✔ Correct procedure.

“NEVER remove the staple. You may photocopy the document while folded, this is not an issue.”This information has been confirmed many times.

4️⃣ Translation of the Apostille Is No Longer Required

This has confused students for years.Previously, the apostille itself also needed translation, but this requirement has now been removed.

✔ New rule.

• Document in Czech → No translation• Document in English → No translation• Document in Turkish → Only the document itself is translated, not the apostille

This saves both time and cost.

5️⃣ How Recent Must the Criminal Record Document Be?

General rule of the Czech Consulate.

📌 Validity period. 90 days(The document must not be older than 3 months.)

6️⃣ Accepted Criminal Record Formats

✔ Accepted.

• e-Devlet PDF printout• Court document with wet signature and stamp• Czech, English, or Turkish (if translated)

❌ Not accepted.

• Phone screenshots• Document with no name• Document with the apostille staple removed• Translation without notary approval (if the document is in Turkish)

(average prices in Türkiye)

If you obtain the document in Czech, all these costs become zero.

8️⃣ Frequently Asked Questions

✔ “Do I need to take the documents in a cardboard folder?”No. A small paperclip is enough.

✔ “Does it need to be printed in color?”No. Black-and-white is accepted.

✔ “Can I email the PDF?”No. A physical printout is mandatory.

✔ “Where do I get the apostille?”At the governorship, district governor’s office, or courthouse.

🎯 In Short

Criminal record and apostille procedures can be completed in 10 minutes when done correctly.The three essential points are.

• Obtain the document in Czech whenever possible• NEVER remove the apostille staple• Bring the document as a printed PDF

If you follow these three rules, the most commonly problematic part of the Czechia long-term Erasmus visa process becomes fully resolved.

One of the biggest challenges for students going to Lithuania for Erasmus is the Migris document upload process.During visa interviews, one frequent question is.

1️⃣ What Is Migris? What Is It Used For?

Migris is the official application platform used by the Lithuanian Migration Department. Through this system you can.

📌 Submit residence permit applications📎 Upload documents🖼️ Upload photos💳 Track payments📅 Manage appointments🔄 Update your application

✔ Issued within the last 10 years✔ Includes the final two pages✔ Photo page must be clearly visible

2) 🏫 Acceptance Letter

✔ Must be in English✔ Start and end dates must be clearly written✔ QR-coded or signed versions are preferred

3) 🏠 Accommodation Document

This is the document students struggle with the most.Accepted accommodation proofs.

• Dormitory housing contract• Rental agreement• University accommodation confirmation email

4) 💶 Proof of Financial Means

Migris requires at least one of the following.

💰 Bank statement📄 Erasmus grant letter📝 Sponsorship letter📂 Family income documents

Students often state in chat groups.“Except for the student certificate, document dates are not very strict.”This means preparing your bank statement a week or two early will not cause issues.

5) 🪪 Photograph (Biometric)

✔ White background✔ 4.5 × 3.5 cm✔ Face must be clear and shadow-free

7) 🎓 Student Certificate

✔ Must be in English✔ The date is extremely important and often checked carefully

3️⃣ How to Upload Documents to Migris. Step by Step

📂 Step 1. Create a Migris Account

✔ Log in to the official site✔ Confirm your email✔ Complete your profile

📝 Step 2. Select “New Application”

Purpose. StudiesType. Temporary Residence Permit

📑 Step 3. Upload All Documents as PDF

✔ Each document must be a single PDF✔ Maximum 5 MB✔ Photos may be uploaded as JPG

⚠️ Step 4. Match the Documents With Your Form Selections

💳 Step 5. Payment

Only card payments are accepted.Students often report.“Revolut works more smoothly.”

📥 Step 6. Download and Save Your Application Summary

Officers may ask for this during the interview.

4️⃣ The Most Common Migris Problems Students Face

❌ 1) Confusion About Document Dates

Students often ask. “How old can documents be?”Answer. Financial documents are flexible in terms of date.

❌ 2) Incorrect PDF Upload

• Uploading multiple files for one document• Uploading photos instead of PDFs• Missing pages

These mistakes slow down your application.

❌ 3) Applying Without Accommodation

Many students struggle to secure dorm rooms (e.g., Sauletekio).At minimum. obtain a temporary accommodation confirmation email.

❌ 4) Migris Application and Appointment Not Matching

Correct order.📌 Complete Migris → Then book appointment

❌ 5) Incorrect Photo Format

Shared directly by students in chat groups. Officers typically ask.

Missing or mismatched uploads lead to additional questions.

Although Migris may seem complicated at first glance, the process flows smoothly when documents are uploaded correctly.Student experiences show that.

One of the most confusing parts of the Czechia Erasmus visa process is the financial documentation.Students constantly ask the same questions.Is the grant sufficient? When is a bank statement required? Is a card photocopy mandatory? How much money needs to be shown?

This guide was prepared to simplify all the confusion seen in student groups and to explain everything clearly.

1️⃣ If Your Grant Is Sufficient, a Bank Statement Is Not Mandatory

The Czech Consulate wants to confirm that the student is financially capable.If your grant meets the minimum amount required by the consulate, no additional bank statement may be requested.

✔ If the grant is sufficient.

  • No additional bank statement

  • No extra proof of income

  • No sponsor required

This has been confirmed in many student groups.Many students received their visas solely with the Erasmus grant.

2️⃣ If the Grant Is Not Enough. Completing the Remaining Amount

Some students receive a lower grant. In this case, the missing amount must be shown in a bank account.

Example.

The logic is simple.

Grant + Bank Statement = Minimum Required Total

3️⃣ Why the Consulate Requests a Card Photocopy

This is one of the most confusing financial requirements.While many countries only ask for a bank statement, Czechia stands out because it also asks for a photocopy of your physical bank card.

✔ Reason.

The consulate wants to verify whether you can actually access the money in your account.

Because.

  • Money may exist in the account

  • But if the card does not work abroad, the student cannot access it

Therefore, the card must show.

  • Your full name

  • International validity

  • Physical card confirmation

4️⃣ Banks That Issue Cards Without Names Are at Risk

Some banks issue cards without a printed name.These cards may be considered invalid by the consulate.

Suggested cards.

  • Papara Metal

  • Ziraat Visa

  • İş Bankası Maximum

  • ING Visa

If your card has no name, request a named card from your bank.

5️⃣ How Much Money Is Enough?

✔ Minimum requirement.

Monthly living cost × number of months you will stay

Usually calculated for 4–6 months.

Average calculations.

A portion is covered by the grant.The remaining amount must be shown by the student.

6️⃣ Showing Extra Money Is Always an Advantage

Due to exchange rate fluctuations, bank fees and account activity, the consulate prefers to see a bit more than the minimum.

Recommended amount.

This makes the application safer.

7️⃣ How Should the Bank Statement Look?

A correct bank statement must include:

✔ Required details.

  • Bank stamp and signature

  • Last 3 months of account activity

  • Account holder’s full name

  • Clearly visible balance

✔ Accepted formats.

  • English bank statement

  • Turkish bank statement, usually accepted

  • PDF printout or original stamped version

An English statement always looks more professional.

8️⃣ Do You Need a Sponsor?

A sponsor is not required, except in cases such as:

  • Very low grant

  • Insufficient personal account balance

  • If the family wishes to document financial support

Documents required from a sponsor.

  • Sponsorship letter

  • Sponsor’s bank statement

  • Proof of income or employment

  • Optional supporting documents

🎯 Summary

Financial documents for the Czechia Erasmus visa are actually quite simple.If your grant is sufficient, the process is easy.If not, you only need to show the missing amount in your account.A card photocopy is mandatory because the consulate wants to ensure you can access your funds abroad.Showing a little extra money strengthens the application.

With the correct documents, financial requirements almost never cause problems in the Czech visa process.

🟦 1. How Much Money Should I Show in the Bank Account?

The Italian Consulate requires a certain minimum daily living cost for long-term visa applications.

This amount can be in a TL account, a Euro account, or a fixed-term or demand deposit account.

❗ Critical information

The money in the account shouldn't be a one-time deposit made for a single day. The consulate prefers to see regular transactions .

🟦 2. What Should a Bank Statement Look Like?

✔ Account activity for at least the last 3 months.

This timeframe is mandatory for most iDATA offices.

The e-government printout is invalid for the bank.

✔ A letter of guarantee is not required.

However, in some cases, it is a document that strengthens the application.

  • If your account activity is weak

  • If the money was deposited at the last minute

  • If you're going to show a sponsor

  • If you are missing your income document

✔ What does a letter of guarantee do?

It is an official document in which the bank guarantees that "this person's money is securely held in the bank" in exchange for X euros .

✔ The most common option

Euro current account → It looks strong and is easy to obtain.

🟦 4. Do I Have to Show a Sponsor?

📌 Who is required to provide a sponsor?

  • Students

  • People without income

  • Unemployed applicants

  • Those whose accounts are deemed insufficient

✔ Mother ✔ Father ✔ Sibling ✔ Spouse ✔ Someone outside the family (if there is a proven link)

✔ Documents that the sponsor must provide

Italy prefers the account to be in the applicant's name.

ab0f79fb-aad0-400e-b2a6-fb4a7986767f.excerpt: Why do phone lines get mixed up in Lithuania? Dual SIM, roaming, SMS, and network problems. — Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant
ab0f79fb-aad0-400e-b2a6-fb4a7986767f.html:
Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant institution.

Many Erasmus students going to Lithuania are encountering SIM card, SMS code, roaming, and network problems. “My SIM card name has changed, I'm not receiving SMS messages, the network keeps showing up as Latvia and Lithuania.” This confusion isn't just about individual devices; it's common in Lithuania due to the operator structure and regional agreements.

In this blog, I've explained the real causes of line interference, dual SIM usage, roaming settings, and the most common solutions students encounter.

Why are Lithuanian operators interfering with each other?

There are three main mobile operators in Lithuania.

  • Telia

  • Bite

  • Tele2

These operators have joint infrastructure agreements among the Baltic countries. Therefore, a Lithuanian SIM card can sometimes connect to a Latvian or Estonian base station. This situation occurs especially in the following cases.

  • When signal strength changes within the campus

  • When there is weak signal in thick-walled buildings

  • When the line is set to automatic network selection

  • When the Roaming Baltic Free agreement is active

That's why students sometimes see "LV" or "EE" operator names on their phones.

Why do problems occur when using dual SIM cards?

Many students' phones support dual SIM cards. This can lead to the following confusion.

  • While roaming is active on the Turkish line, the Lithuanian line can be automatically deactivated.

  • It may become unclear which line the data is identified on.

  • SMS verification messages may try to go to a Turkish phone line instead of a Lithuanian one.

  • Banking apps may send verification verification via the wrong SIM card.

Solution.

  • Manually select the data SIM card.

  • Search SIM card manually select

  • Completely disable data usage on the Turkish line.

  • Operate the Turkish line only in SMS mode.

These four steps will largely resolve the error.

Roaming Issues and Why They Cause Confusion

The most common problems encountered by students wishing to use their Turkish phone line in Lithuania are as follows.

  • The network is constantly changing.

  • The battery drains quickly.

  • Bank SMS messages will not be received.

  • Calls don't go through or there's no sound.

  • The operator connects to the Latvian or Estonian network.

This is because the roaming algorithm selects the strongest signal, which is not always Lithuania.

Solution.

  • Select manual operator

  • Try the 2G, 3G, and 4G options one by one.

  • VoLTE might be disabled on your Türkiye line; check this setting.

The Most Common Phone Problems Experienced by Erasmus Students

Below, I've listed the most common misunderstandings based on the messages in the chat file.

1. Changing the operator name

Students sometimes see "Bite LV" instead of "Bite LT". This stems from the Baltic Sea-wide common network system.

2. SMS codes not arriving

If your Turkish line is in the second SIM slot or in passive roaming, you may not receive SMS messages.

3. Bank applications not performing verification.

It's confusing which line is the active data line.

4. The internet suddenly goes down.

The phone can jump to a different base station.

5. "No service" error even though the SIM card is detected as inserted.

This is common in phones that use dual SIM cards.

SIM Cards That Work Most Reliably in Lithuania

These are the lines that cause the fewest problems, according to student experience.

  • Bite

  • Telia

  • Tele2

Bite is especially popular among students because it is affordable. For example...

  • Free social media quotas

  • Wide coverage

The two operators that cause the fewest problems for Turkish lines.

  • Vodafone

  • Turk Telekom

Turkcell, on the other hand, may experience more network hopping in the Baltic region.

Gold Standard Settings to Adjust in Phone Settings

These settings significantly reduce confusion.

1. Turn off automatic network selection.

Manually select either Bite or Telia.

2. Secure the data SIM card.

Don't let your phone use its data allowance in a variable way.

3. Disable data usage on the Türkiye line.

Only SMS should remain active.

4. Check VoLTE and VoWiFi settings.

It comes disabled by some operators.

5. For those using iMessage and FaceTime

Reactivate the number manually.

Line disruptions are normal and most are easily resolved.

It's quite normal to experience these problems at the beginning of your Erasmus program in Lithuania. The connection will stabilize within a few days.

AEGEE Erasmus Student Society

While ESN is often the first organization that comes to mind when Erasmus and youth mobility are mentioned, there is another important network working for dialogue, integration and personal development among young people across Europe: AEGEE . Founded in Paris in 1985, this student union is one of the largest interdisciplinary student organizations in Europe, politically independent, non-profit and entirely student-run.

Unlike ESN, AEGEE's focus is not only on social events for Erasmus students, but also on promoting European integration, supporting active citizenship, and deepening cultural exchange. Here, we examine everything AEGEE has to offer, along with student experiences and practical tips:

🌐 AEGEE Network and Local Branches (Antennae): Bridges Connecting Europe

  • European Presence: It has branches all over Europe, from large student cities to small towns.

  • Interdisciplinary Approach: Open to students from all fields, whether law, engineering, social sciences, or art. This fosters diverse perspectives and a rich exchange of ideas.

  • Volunteer-based approach: All activities and projects are planned and executed by volunteer students. This provides participants with the opportunity to develop organizational and leadership skills.

📌 Student Experience: "Becoming a member of AEGEE not only brought me new friends, but also gave me experience in organizing events, managing budgets, and working with an international team. Even after Erasmus, I participated in many different projects thanks to the AEGEE network." - Ayşe, Erasmus Graduate from Germany

🎉 Thematic Activities and Projects: Learning and Fun Combined

Although AEGEE organizes parties like ESN, most of its events are based on specific themes and aim to combine entertainment with education.

  • Summer Universities: This is one of AEGEE's most popular and long-standing projects. Every summer, thematic camps lasting 1-2 weeks are organized in different European cities. These camps usually focus on topics such as "Environmental Awareness," "Entrepreneurship," and "Intercultural Communication." Participants both receive training and explore the cultural heritage of the city and country.

  • Conferences & Workshops: They organize conferences, panels, and workshops on various European issues (democracy, human rights, climate change, migration). These events develop students' critical thinking and discussion skills.

  • Youth For Europe Projects: They actively participate in youth projects supported by the European Union and develop their own projects. These projects generally focus on cultural dialogue, European citizenship, and social inclusion.

  • Local & European Events: Local branches organize social events in their respective cities, such as Welcome Week parties, film nights, international dinners, and city tours, while also hosting large-scale conferences and summits at the European level.

🌍 Travel and Cultural Exchange: Not Just a Trip, But an Experience

AEGEE trips go beyond typical tourist tours. The aim is not only to see new places, but also to connect deeply with local culture and engage with different perspectives.

  • AEGEE Network Trips: Students from other branches participate in an event organized by one branch (e.g., a Winter Event or a themed weekend). This offers an opportunity not only to see the place visited but also to share experiences among students from different European countries.

  • Summer Universities: Offer very affordable travel and education opportunities where accommodation and most activity fees are included in the project.

📌 Student Experience: "The 'Democracy in Action' summer university I attended with AEGEE was in Poland. We not only toured Warsaw, but also met with young Polish activists, visited the parliament, and discussed the participation of young people in political processes in Europe. This enriched me both academically and culturally." - Mehmet, Erasmus Student in Italy

🗣️ Personal Development and Leadership Opportunities: Shape Your Future

AEGEE not only provides students with a space to socialize, but also offers invaluable opportunities for personal and professional development.

  • Organization and Project Management: By volunteering to join event or project teams, you will gain skills in planning, budgeting, communicating, and managing an event from start to finish.

  • Leadership Roles: You can take on active roles in local branches or in working groups at the European level. This will develop your leadership, teamwork, and responsibility-taking skills.

  • Intercultural Communication: By constantly interacting with students from different cultures, you develop a global perspective and sharpen your intercultural communication skills.

  • Language Skills: Most activities and projects are conducted in English, providing an excellent environment for practicing English.

👥 AEGEE Community: Connections that Transcend European Borders

AEGEE fosters a strong sense of "European identity" and belonging among its members.

  • Shared Values: AEGEE members are generally young people who value European values, cultural diversity, and active citizenship. These shared values foster strong bonds.

  • Long-lasting friendships: These can go beyond short-term Erasmus friendships like those on ESN; friendships formed at AEGEE events often continue even after university life ends.

  • Professional Network: AEGEE graduates work in diverse sectors across Europe. This can create a valuable professional network for your future career.

✅ Conclusion: What is AEGEE's contribution to the Erasmus and Youth Experience?

Advantages (+):

  • An In-Depth Cultural Experience: Not just about traveling, but about immersing yourself in and learning about the local culture.

  • Personal & Professional Development: Gaining leadership, organizational, and project management skills.

  • European Citizenship Awareness: Gaining knowledge about European integration and youth policies.

  • Unique Travel Opportunities: Affordable and meaningful trips with themed summer universities and events.

  • Strong and Lasting Connections: Gaining a global network of friends with shared interests.

Disadvantages (-):

  • Less "Party" Focused: Compared to ESN, it's more academic and culturally oriented, so it might not meet the expectations of those constantly seeking entertainment.

  • Busy Schedules: Since projects and activities are based on volunteering, it may require dedicating time and effort.

  • May not be as widely known as ESN: It may not be as active or well-known in some universities or cities as ESN.

📌 Final Note: If you want to add academic depth, personal development, and a desire to explore Europe from a different perspective to your Erasmus experience, AEGEE might be perfect for you.

More Information and Directions to Local Branches:

  • AEGEE's main website is: www.aegee.eu

  • To find the AEGEE branch in your city or region of interest: www.aegee.eu/locals

  • For information about AEGEE's summer universities, visit: su.aegee.org

790e1869-d92c-49b7-bfea-e44d168cf36b.excerpt: The Most Common Mistakes Made When Applying for an Italian Visa. With Real-Life Examples. — Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant
790e1869-d92c-49b7-bfea-e44d168cf36b.html:
Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant institution.

An Italian national visa application is perhaps one of the most document-intensive processes in Europe, and even the smallest mistake can lead to rejection. Many applicants, despite believing they have submitted all necessary documents, encounter rejections such as "Article 10. Your purpose of travel has not been sufficiently verified." However, the reason for rejection is often a small, unnoticed error that carries significant meaning for the consulate.

In this guide, you will find: ✔ The most common visa mistakes. ✔ Real application examples. ✔ How to avoid these mistakes. ✔ How the consulate interprets these mistakes, step by step.

🟥 1. Depositing a Large Sum of Money into the Bank at the Last Minute

This is the most common mistake in Italian visa applications, and the one that leads to the most rejections.

❗ Consulate's comment

"This money was borrowed to fund the application. It doesn't reflect your true financial situation."

✔ Solution

  • Use the account actively for at least 3 months in advance.

  • Cash inflows should be regular.

  • Avoid one-time entries from unknown sources.

🟥 2. Faking a 1-Day Stay on Booking or Airbnb

Short-term arranged stays are noticed by the consulate.

❌ Error

Simply show a "fake 1-day booking" for the appointment.

❗ Consulate's comment

"The applicant hasn't arranged any actual accommodation. The plan is unclear."

✔ Real Example

A student studying in Rome only showed a 2-day Airbnb booking. Rejection: Clause 10. Study plan not verified.

✔ Solution

  • Accommodation document for at least 1 month.

  • Dormitory contract, rental agreement, or school accommodation document.

🟥 3. Lack of Proof of Connection with the Sponsor

Simply showing a sponsor is not enough.

❌ Error

Your father is your sponsor, but you have different last names. There's no proof of relationship.

❗ Consulate's comment

"No formal link has been established between the financial support provider and the applicant."

✔ Real Example

The mother, whose surname is different due to divorce, acted as sponsor, but no birth certificate was submitted. Rejection: Article 10. Financial connection could not be proven.

✔ Solution

  • Identity register copy

  • Sponsorship application

  • Income documents

🟥 4. Submitting Incorrect or Incomplete Scholarship Documents

While scholarships are advantageous for students, incorrect documentation is grounds for rejection.

❌ Error

The scholarship document sent by the school lacks a signature or date.

❗ Consulate comment

"The document could not be verified."

✔ Real Example

The scholarship document was submitted as an email PDF. It lacked contact information and a signature. Rejection: Article 10. Educational funding not verified.

✔ Solution

  • Company letterhead

  • Signed and sealed.

  • The date, scholarship amount, and duration must be clearly stated.

🟥 5. Obtaining Your Bank Statement from E-Government

❌ Error

Providing a screenshot of the e-government "bank statement".

❗ Consulate's comment

"This is not an official document. It cannot be verified."

✔ Real Example

An unemployed applicant submitted an e-government printout. It lacked a bank signature. Rejection: Article 10. Financial document unsuitable.

✔ Solution

  • Get a signed and stamped statement from the bank.

  • Transactions from the last 3 months must be complete.

🟥 6. Weak Letter of Intent

The consulate, especially in cases of refusal under Article 10, examines the letter of intent.

❌ Error

"I love Italy. I want to study there," are superficial statements.

❗ Consulate's comment

"The educational objective is not convincing enough."

✔ Real Example

The language school application included a statement of intent consisting of only four sentences. Rejection: Article 10. Purpose of visit unclear.

✔ Solution

  • A letter describing their academic background.

  • The program in Italy contributed to his career.

  • The financial arrangements you planned

🟥 7. Failure to Verify Acceptance Letter

Most schools are official, but some private language schools may not inspire confidence.

❌ Error

The school is not responding to emails.

❗ Consulate's comment

"The acceptance letter could not be verified."

✔ Real Example

The case is pending because a private school in Rome did not answer the phone. Rejection: Article 10. Educational certificate not verified.

✔ Solution

  • Contact the school in advance.

  • Add your contact information to your file.

  • Request a "confirmation letter" from the school.

🟥 8. Discrepancy between Income Declaration and Bank Statement

❌ Error

The sponsor's payroll is high, but their bank account is very weak.

❗ Consulate comment

"Income and bank transactions are inconsistent. Financial situation is uncertain."

✔ Solution

  • The sponsor account must be properly maintained.

  • A statement should be obtained from the payroll account.

  • Additional income documents should be included if necessary.

🟥 9. Incomplete or Incorrect Translation of Documents

❌ Error

The birth certificate is in English. There is no Italian translation.

❗ Consulate's comment

"Foreign documents are invalid."

✔ Real Example

The criminal record certificate was submitted only in Turkish. Rejection: The file could not be processed.

✔ Solution

  • Translations are from a sworn translator.

  • Apostille verification is required.

🟥 10. Providing Incorrect Information During an Appointment

❌ Error

Giving different answers to the question "How long will you stay?".

❗ Consulate comment

"The plan is unclear."

✔ Real Example

The student said they would stay for a year. The accommodation document was valid for three months. Rejection: Inconsistent information.

✔ Solution

  • Documents and verbal statements must be consistent.

⭐ Result

The Italian visa process is one where small mistakes can turn into big problems. The consulate pays close attention to inconsistencies . If you avoid the mistakes we've listed in this guide, your application will be stronger and your chances of rejection will be greatly reduced.

5801bc8f-7605-4940-a3f9-4c222d70f01b.html:
One of the things that surprises students who go to Lithuania on Erasmus is how "strangely peaceful" the nightlife is. A frequently repeated phrase summarizes this: "We drink until dawn, and the atmosphere is still calm." This is no coincidence. Lithuanian pub culture is built on tranquility, order, respect, and social freedom.

In this blog, I've explained step-by-step why pub culture in Lithuania is so relaxed, drawing on student experiences and the local culture.

1️⃣ Quiet and Respectful Social Culture

In Lithuania, people prefer not to speak loudly. You can immediately notice this difference when you sit in a pub.

  • Nobody speaks by shouting.

  • No fighting or arguing is heard between the tables.

  • The music is not loud.

  • People take turns speaking.

This culture of silence is the standard of social behavior in the Baltic countries. Therefore, even the student environment remains calm.

2️⃣ Safe City Structure and Controlled Nightlife

Lithuania is one of the safest countries in Europe. The streets are particularly quiet at night in Vilnius, Kaunas, and Klaipėda.

The main elements that make one feel safe.

  • 👮 Police visibility is high.

  • 🚶 People feel comfortable even when walking alone at night.

  • 💡 The streets are well lit.

  • 🏙 Pub areas are centralized and controlled.

Therefore, students can comfortably spend time outdoors until late at night.

3️⃣ Affordable Prices and Student-Friendly Venues

Pub prices in Lithuania are reasonable compared to the European average. Students especially love these three things.

  • 🍺 Cheap beer

  • 🍟 Snack plates are economical.

  • 🎟 Student discounts

In Vilnius, the Old Town and Užupis areas are both affordable and popular.

4️⃣ Beer as a Cultural Ritual

Lithuania is one of Europe's major beer-producing countries. Beer is not just a beverage, it's also a social ritual.

Characteristics of local beers.

  • Natural ingredients

  • Light to drink

  • It has a sweetish aroma.

  • It usually comes from local producers.

For students, drinking beer is a natural part of conversation, so the atmosphere doesn't become tense or noisy.

5️⃣ Physical Layout of Spaces: Warm, Dim, and Comfortable

The most distinctive feature of Lithuanian pubs is their ambiance and design.

  • 🔥 Dim light

  • 🪑 Comfortable chairs

  • 🎶 Soft music

  • 🕯 Wooden decoration

  • 🧥 Cloakroom culture

These details encourage calmness, and the atmosphere naturally becomes serene.

6️⃣ Social Individuality and Respect for Personal Space

Lithuanians place great importance on personal space, and this influences the pub atmosphere.

  • No one will force their way to your table.

  • Even if you're in a crowd, you won't be disturbed.

  • People stand at handshake distance.

  • Personal boundaries are protected.

This is a positive cultural exchange, especially for students coming from Türkiye.

🎯 In short

In Lithuania, pub culture is more than just "drinking." The combination of silence, respect, safety, low prices, social freedom, and warm venue design naturally creates a peaceful nightlife. Therefore, Erasmus students find going out in Lithuania both fun and relaxing.

  • 🛒 Maxima

  • 🛒 Rimi

Affordable products are readily available, making budget management easier.

4️⃣ Quiet and Safe City Life

Lithuanian cities are quite quiet. Vilnius and Kaunas, in particular, are safe and peaceful at night.

  • 🚶♂️ There is very little noise.

Due to the cold climate, the culture of drinking hot beverages is quite strong. You can find a coffee shop on every corner.

  • ☕ Hot chocolate

  • Uzupis cafes

  • Old Town Pubs

5eb18a33-0446-4ae1-bcd1-3f3cac5bde12.excerpt: Why is the Posta Elettronica Certificata (PEC) (certified e-mail) system important in Italy? — Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant
5eb18a33-0446-4ae1-bcd1-3f3cac5bde12.html:
Confirm the current conditions in writing with the relevant institution.

📩 What is PEC?

PEC stands for Posta Elettronica Certificata , a certified e-mail system. It is a legally valid means of communication in Italy and has the same legal value as registered mail . Every message you send is verified by the system with a receipt for both sending and delivery .

🎓 Why is it important for students and internationals?

  • PEC may be required when you need to send official documents to universities, government agencies, or embassies.

  • Institutions, especially for processes such as registration, scholarships, residence permits, or visa applications, only accept emails from PEC (Process Electronics) addresses.

  • This is the safest and fastest official communication method for students conducting transactions from abroad.

🔧 How to Obtain a PEC Address?

In Italy, you can create a PEC account in minutes through approved providers. You will need to verify your identity (passport or ID card) and enter your tax code ( codice fiscale ).

⚙️ Step-by-Step Guide to Opening a PEC Account

  1. Choose one of the providers above.

  2. Click the “ Attiva PEC ” button.

  3. Upload your credentials.

  4. Enter your Codice fiscale (Italian tax number).

  5. Confirm your account by making a payment.

  6. You now have your own PEC address: → example: yourfirstname.yourlastname@pec.it

🧾 Things to Consider When Sending Emails with PEC

  • Send the email to the recipient's PEC address , not their regular email address.

  • A " Ricevuta di Consegna " (delivery receipt) is automatically sent after each shipment.

  • Keep this receipt, as it serves as legal proof.

  • You cannot send PECs directly through Gmail or Outlook; it is only possible through the PEC provider's web interface or add-in.

💡 Areas of Use for Students

  • University registration and document submission.

  • DSU Toscana, INPS or Questura operations

  • Residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) extension applications

  • Erasmus, scholarship or diploma equivalency documents.

  • Correspondence with public institutions in Italy

🕓 How long does it take to become active?

Once identity verification is complete, PEC is usually activated within 1 hour. Some providers accept online verification with a passport, which speeds up the process.

One of the most frequently asked questions by students applying for Erasmus programs in the Czech Republic is whether to schedule their appointment in Istanbul or Ankara. The approach, speed, flexibility, and document control methods differ significantly between the two cities.

In this blog, I've explained the advantages and disadvantages of Istanbul and Ankara in detail, and which city each student should choose.

1️⃣ Istanbul is recovering faster.

The most frequently mentioned piece of information in conversations is this: When you send an email to Istanbul, they respond the next day. This is a huge advantage, especially when appointments are tight.

✔ Istanbul's speed advantage.

  • Emails are usually answered within 24 hours.

  • Congestion is being managed better.

  • Student circulation is easier because there is more workspace.

  • Urgent applications are processed more easily.

Therefore, Istanbul is a time-saving center for many students.

2️⃣ Ankara is more strict and detail-oriented.

Students' comments about Ankara are almost identical: "They are more meticulous, more strict."

This means this.

  • The documents are examined very carefully.

  • Even the slightest deficiency can cause problems.

  • Flexibility is lower.

✔ What are the advantages?

Applications submitted from Ankara are examined more rigorously, resulting in a better "file integrity" perception. In the Czech system, this sometimes leaves a positive impression.

3️⃣ Istanbul is More Flexible Regarding Documentation

According to the conversations, Istanbul can be flexible with document requirements in some cases. For example...

  • Whether the photocopy is in color or not

  • Acceptance of stapled PDF outputs.

  • Late arriving postal documents

  • Additional documents to be completed.

This makes the application process smoother.

✔ However, an important note

This flexibility only applies during delivery . The final decision rests with the Czech Republic.

4️⃣ The visa issuing authority is the same. The result is not city-dependent.

The most crucial information: The authority that approves Czech Erasmus visas is a single entity : the Czech Ministry of Internal Affairs . Therefore, whether you apply from Istanbul or Ankara, the decision will be made by the same center.

Therefore, when choosing a city for your appointment, you shouldn't think "which country issues the visa?", but rather "which city will cause me the least trouble?".

5️⃣ Which City is More Suitable for You?

✔ You should choose Istanbul, if you want to.

  • If you want to book an appointment faster

  • If you need flexibility

  • If you say there might be minor omissions in the documents

  • If you live far from Ankara

  • If you have a late accommodation document

✔ You should choose Ankara, if you want to.

  • If the documents are complete and fully prepared

  • If you don't mind meticulous control

  • If you live in Ankara

  • If you are closer to the consulate center

  • If you want your documents to "look perfect"

6️⃣ Summary Derived from Real Student Reviews

All the students repeated these two comments.

✔ “Istanbul is fast.”

✔ “Ankara is serious.”

These two sentences explain the whole difference.

🎯 In short

There is no difference between Istanbul and Ankara in terms of "visa outcome" for the Czech Republic Erasmus visa application. The only difference lies in the processing style. Istanbul offers a faster and more flexible process, while Ankara takes a more detailed and disciplined approach. If all documents are complete, Ankara is problem-free, but for students with minor deficiencies, Istanbul is always more lenient.

The Czech Republic long-term visa application form is one of the documents that students most often get stuck on and make mistakes with. The most frequently asked questions are: "How do I fill out the form, how should each section be written, is the Latin alphabet mandatory, are Turkish characters acceptable, and where should I sign?"

This guide is designed to clear up all the confusion.

1️⃣ The form must be filled out using the Latin alphabet.

The Czech Consulate only allows the form to be filled out using Latin characters. Therefore, Turkish characters should not be used.

✔ Correct spelling examples.

  • Şişli → SISLI

  • Cankaya → CANKAYA

  • Göktaş → GOKTAS

It's important to write the name exactly as it appears in the passport, but even if your passport contains Turkish characters, you should write the Latin equivalent on the form.

2️⃣ Filling out the form on a computer is the most accurate method.

Although the consulate accepts manual completion, the most secure method is to fill out the PDF form on a computer . This method...

  • It is more legible.

  • Reduces the risk of errors.

  • Deleting the document will not corrupt it.

Handwritten forms often have legibility issues.

3️⃣ Stapling Prohibited. Forms must not be stapled.

This topic has been frequently discussed in student chats. Application forms should absolutely not be stapled.

✔ The correct method.

  • Secure with a paperclip from the top.

  • Present it in the file if necessary.

If you use a staple, the document may be treated as "processed paper" in some places.

4️⃣ Color print is not required. Black and white is acceptable.

The consulate does not require color printouts. Black and white printouts are perfectly acceptable.

✔ Prevents unnecessary expenses

Most students are wasting money on color printouts.

5️⃣ The signature is placed on the last page. Not every page of the form is signed.

At the end of the form, there is a "Applicant's Signature" section. Only this section should be signed. Signing every page is considered a mistake.

✔ Suggestion

Use the same signature as in your passport.

6️⃣ The Most Confused Areas and Correct Answers

✔ “Place of Submission”

Enter the city you applied from → ISTANBUL / ANKARA

✔ “Purpose of Stay”

STUDY (Long-term)

✔ “Host Institution”

The English name of the university you were accepted to is written here.

✔ “Means of Financial Support”

GRANT + OWN FUNDS (If there is an Erasmus grant, this should be written)

✔ “Accommodation”

The address on the accommodation document must be written exactly as it appears.

✔ “Duration of Stay”

The dates must be exactly the same as those in the acceptance letter.

7️⃣ Using the Correct Form is Very Important

A common mistake mentioned in conversations: some students download and fill out tourist visa forms . This will definitely lead to rejection.

✔ Correct form.

"Long-term Visa Application Form – Czech Republic" (Usually 3 pages long)

8️⃣ Logical consistency is sought in the form.

The consulate wants the form not just to be filled out, but to make sense .

Example.

  • The accommodation start date and arrival date must be the same.

  • The length of stay and the duration of the grant should be compatible.

  • The passport must be valid for a sufficient period.

🎯 In short

Although the Czech Republic long-term application form may seem complex, it only takes 10 minutes if completed correctly. Key points:

  • Using Latin letters

  • Not stapling the form

  • Writing the correct dates

  • Just sign the last page.

If this process is done correctly, the most critical part of the application will be easily completed.

bc05c3ab-6417-4f03-9bc1-b3248c2fbbf9.excerpt: Student Societies Comparison: IC Firenze, ESN, and AEGEE – Which One Is Right for You? — Going abroad with Erasmus or an international exchange program is one of the most exciting

Going abroad with Erasmus or an international exchange program is one of the most exciting experiences of your life. However, adapting to a new country and culture, making friends, and exploring all the opportunities the city has to offer can sometimes be challenging. That's where student clubs come in!

There are many different student organizations on the market. In this article, we will compare a local organization like IC Firenze with well-known European networks such as ESN (Erasmus Student Network) and AEGEE (Association des États Généraux des Étudiants de l'Europe) . Which one best suits your needs?

1. IC Firenze (International Community Florence)

We provided detailed information about IC Firenze in our previous article, but let's review its basic features for comparison:

  • Focus: A local organization, entirely focused on Florence.

  • Mission: To make Florence one of the most attractive cities for international students and to support students throughout their lives in the city.

  • Structure: An apolitical, non-profit association operating on the principle of "student-to-student" assistance.

  • What they offer:

    • IC Card: Discounts at partner venues and advantageous participation in events in Florence.

    • Activities: Special excursions to Florence and its surroundings (Pisa, Siena), city parties, aperitivos, language exchange nights, cultural events.

    • Practical Support: Accommodation guidance, assistance with bureaucratic processes (Codice Fiscale, Permesso di Soggiorno), affordable Italian language courses.

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students visiting Florence who are looking for a vibrant, city-centric social life, and want to benefit from local support and discounts. It offers a more personal and boutique experience.

2. ESN (Erasmus Student Network)

ESN is one of the largest and best-known student organizations in Europe.

  • Focus: It has a large network with more than 500 local branches in over 40 countries across Europe.

  • Mission: To enrich the experiences of Erasmus and other international exchange students in Europe and to ensure their social and cultural integration.

  • Structure: An international, non-profit, volunteer-based network. Each university/city has its own local chapter (e.g., ESN Firenze, ESN Rome).

  • What they offer:

    • ESNcard: This card, valid throughout Europe, offers discounts on international travel (train, bus), accommodation (hostel), airlines, language courses, and local activities (for example, it has partnerships with Ryanair, Flixbus, and Hostelling International).

    • Events: Local branches organize parties, cultural trips, and social events in their respective cities. There are also larger events organized by ESN at national and international levels (e.g., national platforms, EuroTrips).

    • Mentorship Programs: Volunteer local students mentor newly arrived international students on adapting to the city and university.

    • Social Projects: They organize various social responsibility projects and thematic weeks (Health Week, Environment Week, etc.).

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students planning to travel to different cities and countries in Europe, who want to take advantage of international travel discounts, be part of a wide network, and not be limited to Florence.

3. AEGEE (Association des États Généraux des Étudiants de l'Europe)

AEGEE is a European-based organization focused on student integration and personal development, primarily through lobbying and project-based initiatives.

  • Focus: It has local branches in over 130 cities across more than 40 countries. It focuses on European youth and integration.

  • Its mission is to foster the personal development of young people, bring together students from across Europe, promote active citizenship, and contribute to European integration.

  • Structure: A non-profit, volunteer-based, and apolitical youth organization.

  • What they offer:

    • Summer Universities: One of AEGEE's best-known events. These are 1-2 week programs held in different European cities during the summer months, focusing on cultural, academic, or thematic topics. Participants receive training and also participate in social activities.

    • Conferences and Working Groups: They organize seminars, conferences, and working groups across Europe on topics such as youth policies, sustainability, and human rights.

    • Project Management and Lobbying: They work with the European Commission and other organizations to draw attention to the problems of young people and to influence policies.

    • Networking: Offers opportunities to meet young people from different cultures and build long-term international connections.

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students who want to invest in personal development, improve leadership skills, develop projects in areas such as politics, environment or human rights, and build broad international networks, going beyond just parties and trips. While it has a social aspect, it is primarily focused on "development".

Conclusion: Which one should you choose?

Your choice depends entirely on your expectations and goals:

  • If you're only staying in Florence and want to explore the city thoroughly and make the most of what local has to offer, IC Firenze is a great starting point. You'll stay on top of the city's pulse with local discounts and Florence-focused events.

  • If you plan to travel extensively throughout Europe, meet people from different countries, and take advantage of discounts on your travels, you should definitely join ESN . Its wide network and the benefits of the ESNcard will make your Erasmus experience much more economical and enriching.

  • If you want to focus on your personal and professional development, gain knowledge about European issues, and get involved in meaningful projects, in addition to social activities: AEGEE offers you invaluable opportunities. You will broaden your horizons with international conferences and Summer Universities.

Remember, it's possible to be a member of more than one organization! You can get an ESNcard and benefit from travel discounts, attend local IC Firenze parties in Florence, or apply for an AEGEE Summer University program. Most importantly, you can tailor this experience to your own interests!

If you're an Erasmus student embarking on a new adventure in the historic streets of Florence, one of the quickest ways to adapt to the city and its social life is to join student communities. IC Firenze (International Community Florence) , much like ESN (Erasmus Student Network) but entirely focused on Florence and a local, friendly community, can be your biggest support in this regard.

👥 What is IC Firenze? What exactly do they do?

IC Firenze is a non-profit, apolitical student association founded to support international students and Erasmus participants arriving in Florence. Its core principle is quite simple: student-to-student help. Volunteer students who have previously experienced similar situations help newcomers seamlessly adapt to the city, culture, and university life.

  • Local Focus: Unlike an international network like ESN, IC Firenze's entire energy and resources are dedicated to Florence. This allows them to offer a more boutique and focused experience, specific to the city.

  • Their mission: To make Florence one of the most attractive and livable cities for international students, and to support students from the process before their arrival in the city throughout their stay.

💳 The famous IC Card: Your Passport in Florence

What do you get with an IC Card?

  • Event Discounts: You get discounted or sometimes free access to all parties, trips, and events organized by IC Firenze.

  • Venue Deals: You'll receive exclusive discounts at participating bars, pubs (such as popular student hangouts like The Lion's Fountain), restaurants, and pizzerias.

  • Service Discounts: Special offers are available for services such as gyms, travel agencies, and even opening a bank account.

  • Free Drinks: Many parties and events offer cardholders a complimentary "welcome drink".

Is it worth it? If you're a social student and plan on attending at least one or two events a week, the card will easily pay for itself in the first few weeks.

🎉 More Than Just a Party: IC Firenze Event Calendar

IC Firenze has a very wide range of activities that cater to all types of students.

  1. Social and Cultural Activities:

    • Welcome Days/Party: The biggest get-together event at the beginning of the semester, bringing all the new students together.

    • Aperitivo Linguistico (Language Exchange Nights): Relaxed and social gatherings that bring together students who want to practice different languages. Great for improving your Italian!

    • Cultural Dinners: Delicious evenings where everyone brings a dish from their own country and explores world cuisines.

    • Themed Parties: Costume and themed parties for special occasions such as Halloween, Carnival, or end-of-term holidays.

  2. Excursions and Discovery Tours:

    • Day Trips: Bus tours to Tuscan gems such as Pisa, Siena, Cinque Terre, and San Gimignano.

    • Weekend Trips: Overnight trips to larger cities like Rome, Venice, or Milan.

    • Outdoor Activities: Hiking and trekking events organized in the magnificent hills of Tuscany.

🏠 From Accommodation to Bureaucracy: Practical Support

One of IC Firenze's most valuable services is the practical assistance it provides. This support can be a lifesaver, especially for a student arriving in Italy for the first time.

  • Accommodation Support: They provide guidance in finding reliable landlords and apartments. They warn you against rental scams.

  • Bureaucratic Assistance: They guide you through complex processes in Italy, such as obtaining a tax identification number ( Codice Fiscale ) or a residence permit ( Permesso di Soggiorno ), which every student must acquire.

  • Italian Language Courses: Through their partner language schools, they organize affordable Italian lessons for international students.

📞 How to Get There and Join the Community?

It is quite easy to contact IC Firenze and stay informed about their events.

  • Official Website: This should be your first stop for the latest information, event calendar, and card details.

  • Email Address: You can write directly for any questions, suggestions, and support requests.

    • info@erasmusfirenze.it

  • Social Media: Be sure to follow their social media accounts to avoid missing event announcements, photos, and instant updates. Instagram is especially their most active platform.

    • Instagram: @icfirenze

    • Facebook: International Community Firenze

Offices: You can visit their offices, which are usually active at the beginning of the term, to pick up your IC Card and get information in person. Check their website or social media announcements for office addresses and opening hours.

✅ Summary: Should you join IC Firenze?

Advantages:

  • In Florence, you instantly become part of a large and international social circle.

  • With IC Card, you can save a significant amount of money while living in the city.

  • Regular activities will leave you with no chance of getting bored.

  • You receive reliable support during challenging processes such as accommodation and bureaucracy.

Disadvantages:

  • It focuses solely on Florence; it is not part of an international network like ESN.

  • Popular tours can fill up quickly.

In conclusion, if you want to have a fulfilling, social, and hassle-free Erasmus or exchange program experience in Florence, joining the IC Firenze community is one of the best steps you can take. Your first task upon arriving in the city should be to find their "Welcome Day" event!

Application requirements and current sources

The Czech official study-residence procedure publishes a 60-day processing limit. The clock does not run during a lawful suspension; this is not a guarantee of a decision within 60 calendar days. Application routes, document requirements and registration deadlines differ between a long-term visa, a residence permit and a D/VR entry visa. Keep proof of submission and comply with any written request for additional documents. A universal 30-day grace period must not be assumed.

Official source · ipc.gov.cz

If your Czech accommodation document is delayed in the post, act before your visa appointment. Contact the issuer and the competent Czech mission, explain the situation and ask which compliant option is available. There is no universal rule promising Erasmus students 30 extra days, acceptance of an incomplete file or an unchanged processing time. A postal tracking record explains a delay; it does not replace required accommodation evidence.

1. Check which accommodation proof fits your case

The Interior Ministry lists several forms: an accommodation confirmation, a lease or sublease agreement, or proof of ownership. Each has its own requirements. A university or dormitory may issue a confirmation; a private rental can require a valid agreement and evidence of the provider's authority. Ask the issuer for the right document rather than assuming that only one particular posted letter is acceptable. Check names, address and relevant dates for accuracy.

2. Paper, certified copies and electronic documents differ

Official guidance accepts an original or certified copy of a valid lease or sublease agreement. A written accommodation confirmation has its own signature rules and exceptions. A scan printed from an ordinary email is not automatically an original or a certified copy. A blue postal mark is not the universal legal test of authenticity: what matters is the applicable document, authorised issuer, required signature or certification and submission method.

3. Do not confuse electronic routes with consular submission

Current Interior Ministry guidance says that an accommodation confirmation for an application filed at a Czech diplomatic mission abroad must be submitted on paper, not electronically. For applications filed within Czechia, official electronic routes can include a provider's appropriate Data Box or email with a recognised electronic signature. Those arrangements are not permission to replace the consular document with an ordinary PDF. Confirm the applicable route with the authority before relying on electronic delivery.

4. An initial incomplete application can be inadmissible

The study-visa instructions require the prescribed form, fee and all legally required documents at submission. If these requirements are not met, the application can be deemed inadmissible and returned. That is different from a refusal after assessment of a complete application. Do not treat the possibility of later supplementation as a guaranteed right to lodge without accommodation proof. Ask the mission in advance what to do about the existing appointment; do not assume either that attendance without the document is harmless or that you should simply miss it.

5. Follow the actual written deadline if one is issued

Once a procedure is underway, additional documents may be submitted, and an authority may issue a request specifying what to correct and by when. Follow that particular notice and the delivery instructions. Where a Ministry-set deadline can be extended, the official guidance requires a request before it expires; explain the reasons and retain evidence. A request is not automatic approval of an extension. Do not substitute a group-chat claim of “15 or 30 days” for your own notice.

6. Practical steps for a delayed or missing shipment

  • Ask the university or housing provider to confirm the document's issue date, address and tracking reference.
  • Discuss a replacement compliant paper document or appropriate certified copy, and realistic tracked delivery.
  • Send the mission a concise query about the appointment and required form, without unnecessary personal data.
  • Retain official replies, submission receipts and your application reference for any later supplement.
  • If timing affects arrival, ask the host university about genuine late-arrival or enrolment options.

Late or defective evidence can affect admissibility and timing. Processing periods can stop running when legally applicable, including suspension; completing the file does not guarantee a decision by the original travel date. Prepare early and follow the competent authority's current written instructions.

b0f8b75b-988c-4b4a-81dc-d965d002cd45.excerpt: Czech Erasmus Study Visa: Interviews, Language and Appointment Preparation — The Czech official study-residence procedure publishes a 60-day processing limit. The clock does not run during

Application requirements and current sources

The Czech official study-residence procedure publishes a 60-day processing limit. The clock does not run during a lawful suspension; this is not a guarantee of a decision within 60 calendar days. Application routes, document requirements and registration deadlines differ between a long-term visa, a residence permit and a D/VR entry visa. Keep proof of submission and comply with any written request for additional documents. A universal 30-day grace period must not be assumed.

Official source · ipc.gov.cz

“Will there be an interview, and which language will be used?” is a reasonable question before a Czech study visa appointment. Prepare for the possibility of an interview. An Erasmus place does not by itself provide a universal exemption, and another student's brief document handover does not establish the rule for your application. The competent mission's instructions and any subsequent official invitation take priority over anecdotes.

1. First establish whether you need this procedure

This guide primarily concerns third-country nationals applying for a Czech long-term study visa for a stay exceeding 90 days. EU citizens follow a different free-movement framework. Short stays, long-term visas and long-term residence permits are different categories. Some students holding qualifying study permission from another EU Member State can use a mobility route, subject to its conditions. Ask your host university and the official authority which route fits your citizenship, existing status and actual programme; “Erasmus” alone is not the classification.

2. Can an interview take place?

Yes. The Foreign Ministry's general long-term visa guidance describes in-person submission, an interview and fingerprints. The Interior Ministry's study-visa instructions say staff may conduct an interview at submission and may invite the applicant again during examination. Exceptions to personal submission can exist in justified cases; do not assume one applies to you. There is no sound basis for promising that every Erasmus applicant in Istanbul or Ankara will face no questions. Read and answer any official interview invitation.

3. Who examines the application?

The diplomatic mission receives the application, checks the submission and carries out relevant procedural steps. The Ministry of the Interior examines and decides long-term visa applications. This division of responsibilities does not make the consulate a passive collection desk or remove its role in interviews and requests. A short initial appointment also does not mean the examination has finished. Keep the reference number, check official communications and provide requested additions within the specified deadline.

4. Which language should I prepare for?

The Interior Ministry explains that administrative proceedings and their documents use Czech, with officially certified Czech translations of foreign-language documents as required. The language used for practical communication at a mission must be confirmed with that mission. Do not assume a Turkish-speaking officer, the exclusion of English, or a universal ban on Czech. If you need interpreting for a formal act, ask about the required qualifications and arrangements before the appointment. Applicants generally arrange and pay for their interpreter; an accompanying friend may not meet the rules.

5. Istanbul appointments: check the current instructions

The Istanbul Consulate's page updated on 24 September 2026 requires proper email registration for long-term applications and specifies the subject, personal details and PDF attachments. Local jurisdiction must also be respected. Students formally included in the Student Facilitation Programme follow a different route: the Consulate contacts them directly after receiving the programme information. Inclusion is not automatic merely because you are an Erasmus student. Confirm your status with the university and follow the route that actually applies. Check Ankara's own instructions if it is your competent mission.

6. Practical preparation for questions and documents

  • Know your university, programme, dates, intended accommodation and funding arrangements.
  • Check that acceptance, scholarship, bank and housing documents describe a consistent situation.
  • Use the current category-specific checklist for originals, copies, translations and legalisation.
  • Answer truthfully and ask for clarification if you do not understand a question; avoid memorised invented answers.
  • Read a record before signing and raise any misunderstanding through the appropriate interpreter or officer.

These are preparation topics, not an official fixed list of interview questions. A complete file and clear answers do not guarantee approval. Start early, monitor messages after submission and ask the host institution about realistic late-arrival options if necessary.
