For Czech Erasmus students, the most stressful period is waiting for an answer to the question "What is the status of your application?" after submitting it. The mysterious statuses on the Czech Ministry of Internal Affairs website, in particular, confuse students. "Application received," "Assessment," "Pending," "Completed." What do these expressions mean, and which are good and which are bad?

In this blog, I explain all the steps in a simple and clear way.

1️⃣ Where can I check the system status?

Czech Republic long-term visa application status can be checked at this address: 👉 Ministry of Interior (MOI) Visa Application Tracking

Three pieces of information are required for the search.

  • Passport number

  • Date of birth

  • Application type

The inquiry screen displays the result in two seconds.

2️⃣ When will the application be submitted to the system?

This is the point that students get confused about the most. The system is not updated immediately after the application.

✔ Average times.

  • Forwarding from the consulate to the Ministry of Interior. 5-10 days.

  • The file will be processed. 10-20 days.

  • It will appear in the system in 20-30 days.

So the application won't be visible immediately, which is perfectly normal.

3️⃣ Explanation of All Statuses Seen in the System

Now let's move on to the most critical part. I will explain each and every phrase that appears in the system.

🟩 1. “Application Received”

This means your application has been received by the system. No action has been taken yet, but the document has reached the Czech Republic.

This is a good sign.

🟩 2. “In Process” or “Assessment”

It is the longest stage.

At this stage.

  • The documents are checked.

  • Accommodation is confirmed.

  • Financial adequacy is examined.

  • A security and intelligence screening is conducted.

  • Your university acceptance is confirmed.

🟩 3. “Additional Review” or “Pending Documents”

This indicates that there is additional processing required for one of the documents.

Example.

  • Accommodation confirmation

  • Financial control

  • Document readability

The consulate may call you, but most of the time you'll just be asked to wait.

🟩 4. “Processing Completed”

This statement represents the stage where students are happiest.

This indicates that the evaluation is complete . However, a decision may not yet have been announced.

The consulate usually sends an email 1-5 days later. It's most likely confirmation.

🟩 5. “Issued / Approved”

Your visa has been approved. From this moment on, the consulate will begin preparing your passport.

🟥 6. “Rejected / Not Approved”

This is a rare occurrence. In this case, the consulate sends an official decision letter.

4️⃣ Why is the status not updating in the system?

Students often ask, "It's been writing the same thing for a month, is there a problem?"

No. The system updates very slowly.

✔ Reasons for update delays.

  • The files are processed manually.

  • Security checks take a long time.

  • There may be public holidays or high traffic.

  • The inquiry system is not updated for weeks.

Even if the situation doesn't change, the process continues.

5️⃣ What does it mean if the inquiry screen is blank?

This is the most panic-inducing situation: "It looked like my application wasn't there."

This usually happens for the following reasons.

  • The file has not yet been uploaded to the system.

  • The system is undergoing maintenance.

  • Your internet browser is not displaying the page due to a cookie issue.

That doesn't mean there were no applications.

6️⃣ The Healthiest Monitoring Method

✔ Check once a week

Checking it every day creates stress and doesn't strain the system.

✔ Pay attention to emails from the consulate.

The decision usually comes via email.

✔ Don't lose contact with your university.

In some cases, the school expedites the accommodation confirmation process.

Romania Student Visa Guide. The Most Important Part Is Showing Financial Sufficiency Correctly

For Romania, the financial section is the most sensitive part of the student visa. Almost all documents are accepted without issues.However, bank statements, account activity and sponsor letters are where the most mistakes occur.

This guide explains in full detail how students should present their financial situation when applying for a Romanian visa.

1️⃣ How Much Money Should Be in the Bank Account for a Romanian Student Visa?

Romania wants to be sure that the student can support their living expenses.For this reason, a certain minimum amount must appear in the bank account.

Minimum Balance Principle

Basic calculation:

Monthly living cost × duration of stay = minimum required amount

Examples:

This amount can also be shown in local currency.A euro account is not mandatory.

2️⃣ How Should the Bank Statement Look?

Romania places great importance on the bank statement. It must meet the following requirements:

✔ Must have a wet signature from the bankScreenshots from e-government or mobile banking are not accepted.

✔ Account activity must be clean and consistentSudden large deposits appear suspicious.

✔ Last 3 months of transactions must be included

✔ If the balance is in local currency, the embassy will convert it using the daily exchange rate

✔ The account must belong to the studentIf it belongs to a family member, a sponsor letter becomes mandatory.

3️⃣ How Should Students Receiving Erasmus Grants Show Their Finances?

Erasmus grants support financial sufficiency, but the grant letter alone is not enough.

4️⃣ Is a Sponsor Letter Mandatory?

A sponsor letter is not always required, but it becomes necessary in the following cases:

• Insufficient balance in the student’s account• Money located in a family member’s account• The student has no regular income• Account activity does not belong to the student

Typical sponsors:

• Mother• Father• Legal guardian

A sponsor letter should include:

• Sponsor’s personal details• Relationship to the student• Duration of financial support• Support commitment• Signature• Sponsor’s own bank statement attached

Notary approval is optional but adds credibility.

5️⃣ How to Show Money Stored in a Family Account?

A family account alone is not accepted.The embassy assumes the money does not belong to the student.

Therefore these three documents are required:

✔ Sponsor letter✔ Sponsor bank statement✔ Copy of sponsor’s ID

Together, these make the family account acceptable.

6️⃣ Does Depositing Money at the Last Minute Cause Problems?

Yes. Large, sudden deposits are viewed as unreliable.

Embassy concerns:

• Source of funds unclear• Looks like last-minute preparation rather than genuine savings

Correct method:

✔ Funds should already be in the account beforehand✔ Balance should appear stable and consistent

No. TL or any currency is acceptable.

The embassy examines:

• Euro equivalent of total balance• Transaction pattern• Clarity of sponsor support (if any)

Currency is not important, transparency is.

8️⃣ Is a Bank Letter Required?

Some embassy officers request it.

A bank letter usually includes:

• Account holder name• Total balance• Type of account• Latest updated date• Bank stamp and signature

Not mandatory, but strengthens the application.

9️⃣ Most Common Financial Mistakes

• Depositing money last minute• Presenting an empty account with no activity• Submitting a family account without a sponsor letter• Choosing the wrong insurance coverage• Not submitting grant documents• Providing screenshots instead of signed statements• Missing pages in the bank statement

These may lead to refusal or additional processing.

🎯 Summary

If financial sufficiency is shown correctly, the Romanian student visa process goes smoothly.A proper bank statement, consistent account history and a complete sponsor letter (if needed) strengthen the application significantly.

Key points:

• Sufficient minimum balance must be available• Statement must be signed and stamped• Sponsor letter must be complete (if applicable)• Grant letter must be included• Money flow must appear logical and stable

Meeting these conditions makes the financial section of the Romanian student visa much easier to pass.

Spain offers a variety of scholarship programs for international and Spanish students with financial constraints. These scholarships are offered to help students cover the costs of their education. Scholarship Programs in Spain:

1. MEFP Scholarships (Ministerio de Educación y Formación Profesional) :

  • Scholarship Types :

    • General Scholarships : General scholarships to cover students' educational expenses.

    • Tuition Fee Scholarships : Scholarships that help pay for university fees.

    • Relocation and Transportation Scholarships : Scholarships that cover transportation and moving expenses for students studying away from their place of residence.

  • Application Requirements : Depending on family income, students are required to submit documentation demonstrating their financial situation. Additionally, students' academic achievement is also considered.

  • General Information : These scholarships, offered by the Community of Madrid, are available to both Spanish and international students. They are awarded specifically to students with high academic achievement but limited financial means.

  • Application Requirements : A certain level of academic achievement is required to apply for a scholarship. Additionally, students' financial situation and family income are also taken into consideration.

3. Erasmus+ Program :

  • General Information : The Erasmus+ program is a scholarship program funded by the European Union that provides students with the opportunity to study at various universities in Europe. It is open to both Spanish and international students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Student Mobility : Scholarships that allow students to study in another European country for a certain period of time.

    • Internship Mobility : Scholarships that allow students to do internships abroad.

  • Application Requirements : Erasmus+ scholarships are awarded based on academic achievement and financial standing. Students must also meet the requirements of their chosen program.

  • General Information : These scholarships, offered by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), are aimed at international students, particularly those from Latin America, Africa, and Asia. They provide financial support to students wishing to pursue postgraduate studies in Spain.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships offered to international students enrolled in postgraduate programs.

    • Doctoral and Research Scholarships : Scholarships for international students enrolled in doctoral programs and students conducting research projects.

  • Application Requirements : Factors such as students' academic success level, income status and the quality of their research projects are evaluated.

5. La Caixa Scholarships :

  • General Information : These scholarships, offered by La Caixa Foundation, are available to international and Spanish students enrolled in undergraduate and graduate programs in Spain. They are awarded specifically to students experiencing financial hardship and demonstrating academic achievement.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Undergraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for students pursuing undergraduate studies in Spain.

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships offered to students pursuing master's and doctoral studies in Spain.

  • Application Requirements : Students' academic success, financial situation and the requirements of the programs they apply for are taken into consideration.

Scholarship programs in Spain offer significant support to students with limited financial means. These scholarships provide many students with the opportunity to receive a quality education in Spain, significantly reducing their educational expenses.

DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) scholarships are a scholarship program for international and Italian students in Italy who are financially disadvantaged. DSU scholarships are provided to help students cover the cost of their education and are administered regionally. These scholarships offer a variety of financial assistance options, including tuition waivers, accommodation support, meal assistance, and financial support for books and other educational materials.

Key Features of DSU Scholarships:

  1. Scope of the Scholarship :

    • Tuition Fee Exemption : Students who win the scholarship may be exempt from university tuition fees.

    • Accommodation Support : Students can benefit from free or discounted accommodation in university dormitories.

    • Meal Assistance : Free or discounted meals are provided in university cafeterias.

    • Educational Material Support : Financial support may be provided for books, educational materials and other academic needs.

    • Scholarship Payment : The scholarship amount varies depending on the student's financial situation, academic achievement, and the decision of the regional DSU office. Scholarship payments are generally made in two installments.

  2. Application Conditions :

    • Financial Status : The applicant's family income must be below a certain threshold. Income and assets are proven through the ISEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente).

    • Academic Performance : Students are required to maintain a certain level of academic achievement. This level of achievement may vary by university and department.

    • Citizenship and Residency : International students studying in Italy are also eligible to apply for DSU scholarships. However, they may be required to have regular residence in Italy.

    • Student Status : Scholarships are generally available to full-time students. Different conditions may apply to part-time students.

  3. Application Process :

    • Regional Administration : DSU scholarships are administered regionally in Italy. Therefore, scholarship applications should be submitted to the DSU office in the region where the student studies or resides.

    • Application Deadlines : The application process usually begins in the summer months, and students must complete the relevant documents and submit them by the application deadline.

    • Required Documents : The following documents are generally required for the application: İSEE document, academic transcript, ID and residence permit (for foreign students), documents showing family income and assets.

    • Announcement of Results : Application results are generally announced at the beginning of the academic year. Students who have won a scholarship are informed of the scholarship amount and terms and conditions.

  4. Continuity of Scholarship :

    • Academic Performance : Maintaining academic success is essential for the scholarship to continue. A certain number of credits may be required and satisfactory exam performance may be required.

    • Change in Income Situation : If there is a significant change in the income situation of the student or their family, the scholarship may be re-evaluated and this may affect the scholarship amount.

  5. Additional Benefits and Supports :

    • Study Abroad Support : Some DSU scholarships also provide support to students participating in study abroad programs such as Erasmus.

    • Additional Aid : Additional aid may be provided to students who are in a much worse financial situation or additional scholarships may be provided for special circumstances.

DSU Scholarship Benefits:

  • Accessibility : DSU scholarships cater to a wide range of financially disadvantaged students and provide equal educational opportunities.

  • Various Supports : Helps students go through the learning process more comfortably by greatly reducing their education costs.

  • Regional Support : Administering scholarships regionally ensures that students receive support based on needs in their area.

DSU scholarships also offer a great opportunity for international students looking to study in Italy. Taking advantage of these scholarships can significantly reduce the cost of studying in Italy and help students achieve their academic goals.

Scholarship Programs in Germany:

1. DAAD Scholarships (Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst - German Academic Exchange Service) :

  • General Information : DAAD is one of Germany's largest scholarship providers. It offers a wide range of scholarships for both German and international students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees. These scholarships are typically fully comprehensive and cover expenses such as tuition fees, living expenses, and health insurance.

Additionally, some scholarships require proof of a specific language proficiency (usually English or German).

2. Deutschlandstipendium :

  • General Information : This scholarship program is jointly funded by the German government and the private sector. Available to both German and international students, it provides financial support as well as a variety of career development and mentoring opportunities.

  • Application Requirements : During the application process, students' academic achievement, social responsibility, and personal development are evaluated. Furthermore, students' financial situation and needs are also taken into consideration.

3. Friedrich Ebert Stiftung Scholarships :

  • General Information : The Friedrich Ebert Foundation is a foundation that offers scholarships to promote social justice and democratic values. It specifically awards scholarships to socially disadvantaged students who demonstrate academic achievement.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Undergraduate and Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for international students pursuing undergraduate and graduate studies in Germany. These scholarships cover tuition fees, living expenses, and study materials.

    • PhD Scholarships : Scholarships for students who want to pursue a PhD in Germany.

Read the call as an eligibility checklist before collecting certifications or paying application expenses. Introduction: One of the first problems with Erasmus – the telephone line

One of the most common problems for students traveling to Italy for their Erasmus studies is finding a telephone line and internet package . Using a Turkish phone line can be expensive and unsuitable for official transactions. This guide explains how to get a telephone line in Italy, which providers are best, prices, and other tips to keep in mind.

Why should you have a local connection in Italy?

  • Roaming charges are very high → Using a Turkish connection will put a strain on your budget in the long run.

  • Requirement for banking and official transactions → Universities, banks and consulates often require an Italian number.

  • Easy communication with friends and hosts → Using a local line makes everyday life easier.

The most common operators in Italy

The main GSM providers you can choose in Italy are:

  1. TIM (Telecom Italia Mobile) – The oldest and most widespread operator in the country.

  2. Vodafone Italia – Offers a strong infrastructure, especially in large cities.

  3. WindTre – Affordable rates for students.

  4. Iliad – Popular with its new generation, affordable and transparent tariffs.

  5. PosteMobile – the low-cost line of the Italian post office.

Documents required to obtain a line

The following documents are usually required to obtain a SIM card:

  • Passport or identity card if you are an EU citizen

  • Codice Fiscale (tax number) – most operators require this

👉 Note: You can get the Codice Fiscale online from Turkey or pick it up at the Agenzia delle Entrate office after your arrival in Italy.

Average student packages:

Example tariffs:

Where can I buy a SIM card?

  • Operator stores: TIM, Vodafone, and WindTre stores are frequently found in city centers.

  • Airports: Easy to reach on the first day, but prices are slightly higher.

  • Post offices: For the PosteMobile line.

  • Apply online: Some providers can deliver the SIM card to your address.

What you should pay attention to

  • Be sure to keep a copy of your passport with you.

  • Packages renew automatically and are debited from your bank account or prepaid balance.

  • Check the coverage in the city you are in.

  • English may not always be spoken in shops, so learning simple Italian phrases will make things easier.

  • Short-term stay (1–3 months): Iliad is affordable and convenient.

Diploma

Getting a phone line in Italy is easy. However, choosing the right provider depends on your budget and usage habits . Application requirements and current sources

For university-enrolment student visas in academic years 2026–2027 and 2027–2028, Italy’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs states an annual minimum financial requirement of EUR 10,179.85. This figure does not automatically apply to every study-visa category: other study purposes follow the official subsistence table and duration of stay. Distinguish an entry visa from a residence-permit renewal. The ministry does not accept a bank guarantee or surety insurance as a substitute for the required financial evidence.

Official source · www.esteri.it

For non-EU students in Italy, the health coverage required for a residence permit must cover the study or mobility period. Bologna University states that a private policy must be in your name, valid in Italy and cover illness, accidents and maternity. Do not treat a first-15-days travel policy as sufficient for the whole study stay. A residence permit cannot outlast the health coverage. Private insurance and SSN registration are distinct options; confirm the coverage accepted for your case.

Official source · www.unibo.it

Types of Erasmus visas for Italy

The most frequently requested visas for students going to Italy under the Erasmus program are:

  • National visa type D (for periods exceeding 90 days): Used for Erasmus study or internship programs.

  • Schengen Visa Type C (up to 90 days): Valid for short internships or exchange programs.

👉 If you have a green passport and your stay does not exceed 90 days, you may not need a visa. (Depending on the number of days)

Visa application process

  1. University pre-registration: Pre-registration for the training program is required.

  2. iDATA Application: Italy visa applications from Turkey are accepted via iDATA.

  3. Consular appointment: Documents are submitted and biometric data is collected.

  4. Waiting for results: It can take an average of 4 to 8 weeks and during busy periods it can take longer.

The following documents are generally required for a visa application:

  • Passport (valid for at least 6 months from the return date)

  • Letter of admission – must be obtained from the university

  • University admission

  • Proof of accommodation (dormitory, rental agreement or hotel reservation)

  • Proof of financial situation (bank statement, sponsorship letter, Erasmus scholarship)

  • Biometric photo

  • Flight reservation (one-way flights are also possible, but a round-trip flight is usually required)

👉 Some documents may require translation into Italian or English . Documents such as civil registry extracts and student certificates may require notarized translations.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Where can I view the rejection/admission letter from Universitaly? → It can be tracked on the platform and will also be sent via email.

  • How long does it take to receive the visa results? → On average, it takes 1–2 months, but this varies depending on the season.

  • Are any additional documents required for the internship? → The acceptance letter must include the note "Internship/Traineeship."

Tips and advice

  • Start preparing documents early ; translation and notary procedures take time.

  • Please check the iDATA system regularly , as appointments at the consulate fill up quickly.

  • Be sure to include it in your Erasmus scholarship documents; it will strengthen your financial strength.

  • You must apply for a residence permit ( Permesso di Soggiorno ) in Italy within 8 days of receiving the visa.

Applying for an Erasmus visa for Italy is easy if you have all the necessary documents prepared and follow the procedures correctly. It's important to submit your application on time and all the required documents. Since the consular and iDATA processes can be time-consuming, early planning is a great advantage.

Why is money management important in the Erasmus program?

One of the most frequently asked questions among Erasmus students traveling to Italy concerns opening a bank account, transferring money, and conducting everyday financial transactions . While Turkish debit cards are useful for short-term use, opening a local bank account for longer stays reduces costs and simplifies official transactions.

Should you open a bank account in Italy?

  • For short-term (1-3 months) Erasmus or internship programs → international cards from Turkish banks (Wise, Revolut, Papara, Ziraat Bank, İş Bank Eurocard) are usually sufficient.

  • For long-term Erasmus programs (6-12 months), opening a bank account in Italy is almost essential. Because:

    • The Erasmus scholarship can be paid directly into the Italian account.

    • The landlord/agency can request rent payments through the local account.

    • You are exempt from foreign currency deductions on daily expenses.

Cheap banks for students in Italy

There are many large banks in Italy, but students generally choose these options:

  • UniCredit Bank: One of Italy's largest banks offers special account types for students.

  • Intesa Sanpaolo: Extensive branch network and low-commission account options available for students.

  • Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena: A historic bank that may offer attractive special offers for Erasmus students.

  • Poste Italiane (Postepay): Card and mobile banking solutions for students who do not want to open a bank account.

  • Online banks (N26, Revolut, Wise): Fast setup, low costs, multi-currency support.

👉 N26 and Revolut are especially popular with students because an account can be opened in minutes and the physical card is sent to your address.

Documents required to open a bank account

To open a bank account in Italy, the following documents are required:

  • passport

  • Codice Fiscale (tax number)

  • Certificate of study / Erasmus admission letter

  • Proof of address (dormitory contract, rental agreement or temporary hotel registration)

👉 Some banks may not allow you to open an account until you have received a residence permit (Permesso di Soggiorno) .

Daily financial transactions

  • Card use: Cash use is declining; cards are accepted almost everywhere. However, cash may be required in small cafes or at train stations.

  • Money transfer: Apps like Wise and Revolut are much cheaper than bank transfers.

Suggestions for students

  • Pay your Erasmus scholarship directly into your Italian account and avoid losses due to the TL/€ exchange rate difference.

  • For longer stays you can choose UniCredit or Intesa Sanpaolo .

  • For those looking for a more practical solution, N26 or Revolut are fast and student-friendly.

  • Always carry some cash with you. Cards may not be accepted everywhere, especially in smaller towns.

  • When opening a bank account, be sure to ask whether there are any account maintenance fees .

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Is a euro account opened in Turkey sufficient? → Yes, for short-term Erasmus stays, but for longer stays, a local account is more advantageous.

  • Is opening a bank account mandatory? → No, but it is recommended for your Erasmus grant and rent payments.

  • Can I open a bank account without a fiscal code? → Most banks require it, but some online banks (like N26) can process transactions without it.

Managing your finances as an Erasmus student in Italy can seem complicated at first. However, choosing the right bank or applying online makes things much easier. International cards are the best solution for short stays , while a local bank account is recommended for longer stays.

The informed consent form (INF) is crucial for informing participants in clinical trials and protecting their rights. In this article, we explain step-by-step how to create such a form.

1. Determine the purpose of the form

The informed consent form is designed to provide volunteer participants in clinical trials with comprehensive information about the research and obtain their consent. The primary purpose of the form is to protect the rights of volunteers, ensure their participation in the study, and inform them of all potential risks throughout the process.

2. Know your target audience

The language of the form should be appropriate for the target audience, i.e., clear and free of medical jargon. The educational level, age group, and possible medical history of the volunteers should be taken into account. Especially in the case of children, parents or guardians should also be informed.

3. Identify the parts of the form

The BGOF should contain the following main sections:

  • Name and purpose of the research: It should explain what the research is, what its purpose is, and how long the volunteer's participation will last in accordance with that purpose.

  • Volunteer rights: It should be emphasized that the volunteer has the right to withdraw from the research at any time and that doing so will not result in any penalties or loss of rights.

  • Treatment and methods: The treatments to be used in the study, the procedures to be performed on the volunteer, and possible invasive methods should be explained.

  • Risks and side effects: The risks and discomforts that the research subject may be exposed to should be clearly stated. If the research is conducted on pregnant women or children, the specific risks for these groups should also be stated.

  • Alternative treatment options: The patient should be informed of other treatment options and their potential benefits and risks.

  • Confidentiality and data protection: It should be explained how the identity of volunteers will be protected and that their identity will be treated confidentially if the research results are published.

4. Provide detailed information

Each section of the form should contain sufficient explanations so that subjects understand exactly what they are consenting to. In particular, risks, side effects, and the subject's responsibilities should be clear and unambiguous.

5. Explain the volunteer’s rights

The subject's rights, such as the right to withdraw from the study, confidentiality of their identity, and compensation, should be clearly explained. Oral explanations should be provided to ensure the subject fully understands these sections.

6. Collect signatures from the research team and volunteers

The final section of the form must contain the signature of the subject who has been informed of their participation in the study. The signatures of the researcher who informed the subject and, if applicable, any witnesses must also be obtained. For pediatric patient groups, the signatures of the parents or guardians are also required.

7. Make special arrangements for pediatric studies

When conducting research with children, the information and consent process should be adapted to the child's age group. Written informed consent forms should be prepared for children 9 years and older, and written consent should be obtained for children aged 3 to 8, if possible.

8. Revise and approve the form

The completed form must undergo several review processes to ensure its accuracy and completeness. Each page of the form must contain the date, version, and page number. After revision, the form must be submitted to the relevant authorities for approval.

9. Present the form to the volunteer

Finally, make sure the volunteer understands all the details when you present the form. Answer any questions the volunteer may have and provide additional explanations if necessary. After the volunteer signs the form, give them a copy and keep a copy for your records.

10. Make sure the form is constantly updated

It is important to inform subjects of any new information or changes that may arise during the research period and to update the form. Make any necessary updates to the form based on the new information and repeat this process if consent needs to be obtained again.

By following these steps, you can prepare the informed consent form (IFR) and ensure that volunteers participate in the research in an informed manner (FIND IT IN KAD-DD-13_IFR…). https://www.titck.gov.tr/faaliyetalanlari/ilac/klinik-arastirmalar

What are the Portal Login Problems?

The most common mistakes made by students in groups are:

  • Access to the site is blocked: The portal cannot be accessed from Turkey or other countries.

  • Login method error: Students who do not know that “Credentials” should be used instead of “SPID” are receiving an error.

  • Tax code (Codice Fiscale) issue: An error occurs when the wrong identification number is used when logging into the system.

  • Page not opening / white screen: The portal may crash, especially during busy application periods.

Site Unreachable

Issue: Some students are unable to access the DSU Toscana portal directly from Turkey or abroad. The site either fails to load or displays a white screen error.

Solution:

  • Use VPN:

    • Set your location to Italy or one of the EU countries (Germany, Netherlands, France) .

    • Free VPN recommendations: ProtonVPN, Windscribe.

    • For a more stable connection, paid options (NordVPN, ExpressVPN) can be used.

  • Clear Browser Cache: Clear history and cookies in Chrome or Firefox.

  • Try a Different Browser: Safari or Edge sometimes connects to the portal faster.

Using the Wrong Option

Issue: Many students mistakenly click the SPID (Italian digital identity system) option on the DSU Toscana login screen. Since most Erasmus students don't have a SPID, the system throws an error.

Solution:

  • On the login screen , select “Credentials” (Username/Password).

  • Use the username and password DSU gave you before applying.

  • If you have a temporary Codice Fiscale (tax number), write it down correctly.

👉 Remember: Erasmus students generally have to log in with their Credentials .

Errors Related to Codice Fiscale

Problem: Students enter their Turkish ID number or passport number instead of their Codice Fiscal when logging in. The system does not recognize these numbers.

Solution:

  • Before you travel to Italy, request a temporary Codice Fiscale from your consulate or university.

  • Enter letters and numbers with caution, paying attention to upper/lower case sensitivity.

  • If you have lost your Codice Fiscale, you can request it again from the Agenzia delle Entrate.

System Crash During Application Period

Problem: During peak periods, the portal gets overloaded and the page doesn't open.

Solution:

  • Check appointment availability through the competent authority’s current channels. There is no general guarantee that new places will appear at a particular day or time. Protect your application details and do not rely on unverified intermediaries promising a guaranteed result.

  • Do not leave your application to the last days.

  • Even if you get an error in the portal , take a screenshot . You can email proof to the DSU office if needed.

Email Confirmation Problem

Problem: After completing the application, no email confirmation is received. Students are unsure whether their application has been accepted or not.

Solution:

  • Even if the "submit completed" message does not appear on the screen where you complete the application , the application number will still appear in the system.

  • Take a screenshot of this screen.

  • Even if you do not receive an e-mail, if it appears in the system, your application has been recorded.

General Recommendations ✅

  • The combination of VPN + Credentials is the solution that works best.

  • Choose Google Chrome or Firefox ; do not log in from a mobile browser.

  • Prepare documents in advance , do not leave them to the last minute.

  • Take screenshots at each step.

One of the most confusing points for students applying for DSU Toscana scholarships and accommodation in Italy is how to translate documents. "Is translation alone sufficient for social security statements, bank statements, and lease agreements, or do they absolutely require notarization and apostille?" is a question that comes up in almost every student group.

In this article, we explain in detail the most common document-related problems and solutions.

Which Documents Are Required?

The following documents are generally requested during the application:

  • Social Security Institution service statement / income document

  • Bank statements (annual average balance + year-end balance)

  • Lease contract (for students living in rented accommodation)

  • Tax certificate / income documents (according to family income status)

  • Pension statement (for retired families)

  • A certified copy of the civil registration record → An official document showing the family members and their marital status. The number of family members is especially important when calculating scholarships.

Situations Where Translation Is Sufficient

For some documents, only a sworn translator's translation may be sufficient.

  • Only translation is acceptable unless the university or DSU office explicitly requests “notarization + apostille”.

  • Especially for standard documents such as the Social Security Institution service statement, sometimes translation alone is sufficient.

👉 However, this may vary from university to university and region to region .

Documents Requiring Notary + Apostille

According to most students, the safest way is to submit documents with both notarization and apostille certification .

  • Bank account statements → usually notary + apostille is required.

  • Lease contract → the document that causes the most problems; translation alone may not be sufficient.

  • Pension statement → Since it is a regular income document, notary + apostille is often required.

👉 An apostille ensures your documents are valid abroad. It can be easily obtained from district governorships or provincial governorships in Turkey.

The Most Common Mistakes Students Make

  • Just getting a translation and forgetting to add a notary and apostille

  • Submitting documents with incomplete dates (e.g., only a mid-year statement)

  • Acting with the logic of "they accepted it last year" without receiving clear information from the university

  • Having the translation done by a simple translation office instead of a sworn translator

Solution Suggestions ✅

  • Always check the official band call sheet. It's clearly stated there.

  • If you are not sure → presenting it with a notary + apostille is the safest way.

  • Make sure to have your documents translated by a sworn translator.

  • Try to get written confirmation from your university's international office.

  • Start the process at least 2-3 weeks in advance when preparing the documents.

The clear answer to the question, "Is a translation sufficient, or is a notary and apostille required?" is: It depends on the official summons. However, if you prefer not to take risks, have all your documents prepared with a notarized translation and apostille certification . This way, you can minimize the risk of encountering problems due to missing documents during your application.

The essential rule for the acceptance of rental agreements and title deeds in DSU Toscana applications: 👉 Sworn translation + Apostille + Notary approval + Apostille ).

An Overview of the Permesso di Soggiorno

The Permesso di Soggiorno is the official residence permit in Italy for non-European Union citizens. This document is mandatory for a legal stay exceeding 90 days in the country and also enables individuals to access various social services in Italy. For students, in particular, this document is a fundamental prerequisite for pursuing their education within a legal framework.

The application process consists of four main stages, which may seem complex but are manageable when the correct steps are followed:

  1. Pre-Application Stage: Gathering all necessary documents and obtaining the application kit known as "Kit Giallo."

  2. Form Filling Stage: Diligently, completely, and accurately filling out Modulo 1 within the kit.

  3. Post Office Application Stage: Submitting the filled kit and relevant documents to the post office to complete the initial application process and receive the crucial document called "Ricevuta."

  4. Police Headquarters (Questura) Appointment and Card Delivery Stage: Attending the appointment at the relevant police headquarters on the date provided by the post office, providing biometric data, and collecting the residence permit card.

Each stage of the process requires meticulous attention, as even a minor error can cause the application to be halted or rejected. This report aims to detail this process from start to finish, minimizing potential problems applicants may encounter.

Basic Information: Understanding the Italian Immigration System

What is a Permesso di Soggiorno?

A Permesso di Soggiorno is an official residence document issued to foreigners who wish to reside legally in Italy. This document is granted to individuals who intend to stay in Italy for work, study, family reunification, or other specific purposes. The duration of the document varies according to the purpose of the application. The permit issued for students is called a "Studio" permit and is generally valid for the duration of an academic period.

Essential Italian Terms Glossary for Applicants

  • Kit Giallo (Yellow Kit): This is the yellow-striped application package, obtained free of charge from post offices, which is necessary for the residence permit application. It contains the application forms (Modulo 1 and 2) and payment receipts.

  • Codice Fiscale (Tax Code): A personal, 16-digit Italian tax identification number. It is mandatory for many official transactions in Italy, including residence permit applications.

  • Ricevuta (Receipt): A critical document issued after the post office application, containing the appointment date, time, and the address of the police headquarters (Questura). This document serves as temporary proof of legal status until the official residence permit card is issued.

  • Questura (Police Headquarters): The police unit where residence permit applications are reviewed in the final stage, where fingerprints are taken, and where the card is delivered.

  • Sportello Amico (Friendly Counter): Counters located within post offices, specifically designated for administrative services such as residence permit applications.

  • Rilascio (First-Time Application) and Rinnovo (Renewal): Two important terms referring to application types. Students will mark the Rilascio option for their first application, and Rinnovo for subsequent applications.

The Two-Stage Structure of the System

The two-stage structure of the Italian residence permit application process, involving both the post office and the police headquarters (Questura), might seem like an unnecessary repetition to some applicants. However, this structure is actually designed for efficient and secure process management. Post offices, through their Sportello Amico service, act as widespread and accessible first points of contact. This stage is used for preliminary document checks and collection of necessary fees. Applicants submit only photocopies of their documents, not the originals, at this stage.

The actual and final legal verification process takes place at the police headquarters. The police headquarters collects the applicant's fingerprints to record biometric data and examines the originals of all documents submitted with the application to confirm their legal validity. This two-stage system reduces the workload on post offices while ensuring that security and legal approval are carried out only by authorized law enforcement units. The submission of photocopies at the post office stage and the request for originals at the police headquarters stage is a natural part of this process.

Stage 1: Pre-Application Preparation and Document Collection

Obtaining and Contents of the Kit Giallo

The first step of the application process is to obtain the Kit Giallo free of charge from any post office branch that has a Sportello Amico counter. This kit comes in a yellow-striped envelope and contains the forms necessary for the residence permit application (Modulo 1, Modulo 2) and payment receipts (Bollettino).

Student Document Checklist: A Meticulous Guide

One of the most critical steps in the application process is the complete and accurate preparation of all required documents. It is imperative that the documents are consistent with each other and form a legal logical chain. The following list details the documents a student must prepare for a residence permit application:

Each of these documents ensures that the application progresses in a logical chain. For example, a D-type visa legalizes a person's entry into Italy, while documents such as the university acceptance letter and proof of financial means were previously submitted for obtaining this visa. The residence permit application aims to re-submit this previously verified information, proving the purpose and sustainability of the stay in Italy. Inconsistencies between these documents, for example, insufficient proof of financial means, can lead to the failure of the entire application process.

Stage 2: Form Filling - Section by Section Guide

General Rules for Form Filling

The form-filling process is one of the most error-prone parts of the application and requires careful attention. A small inaccuracy can prevent the file from being processed. The basic rules to follow when filling out the form are:

  • Only a black ink pen should be used.

  • All information must be written in capital letters.

  • Each character must be written in a separate box, and one box should be left blank between words.

Filling Out Modulo 1: A Special Guide for Students

Students are required to fill out only Modulo 1 within the Kit Giallo for their application. Modulo 2 is designed for employed individuals with income in Italy and should not be filled out by students. The sections of the form that need to be filled are:

  • Sezione 1: Tipo di richiesta: In this section, the type of application is indicated. If students are applying for the first time, "Rilascio" (First Application) and "Permesso di soggiorno" options should be ticked.

  • Sezione 2: Dati sull'istanza: This section should be filled out last. It must include the total number of filled form pages and attached A4-sized documents.

  • Sezione 3: Dati anagrafici: Surname and first name information must be written according to the passport details. If Codice Fiscale is available, it is added here. Gender (M or F) and marital status (A or B) are indicated with single-letter codes.

  • Sezione 4: Residenza/domicilio in Italia: The valid residence address in Italy must be written in full. This address must be in the same province as the police headquarters to which the application is made.

  • Sezione 5: Dati del titolo di soggiorno (For Renewal): This section is only applicable for those renewing their residence permit, and first-time applicants should leave this section blank.

  • Sezione 7: Permesso di Soggiorno/Motivo del soggiorno: The purpose of the stay in Italy is specified. For students, the purpose is "Studio." The appropriate code for this purpose is "24-study (university courses)."

The sections of the form are tools used by the Italian state to categorize applicants into the correct administrative categories. The fact that Modulo 1 is specific to students and Modulo 2 to employees indicates that the system has different legal requirements and tracking mechanisms for each application type. Filling out the wrong module or entering an incorrect code will place the application into an incorrect legal category from the start, leading to its rejection.

Stage 3: Application Process

Post Office Procedure

Once all forms and documents are ready, the Kit Giallo envelope should be taken unsealed to a post office with a Sportello Amico counter and submitted. After checking the documents, the post office official will collect the payments and issue the "Ricevuta," the most important document related to the application, to the applicant.

Detailed Breakdown of Application Fees

The residence permit application is subject to various fees. These fees are paid at the post office during the application and may vary depending on the application type and duration.

Importance of the Ricevuta

The Ricevuta is much more than a simple receipt. It is an official document proving the successful submission of the application and provides the applicant with a temporary legal status during the most critical stage of the application process, i.e., when the residence permit card has not yet been printed. This document not only proves that the applicant continues to stay legally in Italy but also makes it possible to travel to Turkey or another European Union country. Losing the Ricevuta is extremely risky as it would eliminate appointment information and temporary legal status.

Stage 4: Questura Appointment and Card Delivery

Preparation for the Questura Appointment

The applicant must go to the police headquarters at the address written on the Ricevuta on the date and time specified on it. The appointment should not be missed, and one should absolutely not go to a different address. The documents to be brought to this appointment are:

  • Original of the Ricevuta.

  • Originals of all application documents, including passport and visa.

  • Photocopies of documents submitted to the post office.

  • Two identical, recently taken passport-sized photos.

Fingerprinting Process and Beyond

The appointment primarily involves taking fingerprints and checking the originals of the documents. After the fingerprinting process is completed, the only thing the applicant needs to do is to wait for the residence permit card to be issued. This waiting period can take an average of 6 months.

Information regarding the preparation of the residence permit card is sent via SMS to the mobile phone number provided during the application. When the message arrives, the applicant goes to the police headquarters again and collects their card, accompanied by the Ricevuta document.

The entire process, from the form-filling stage to the SMS notification, still largely relies on a manual and paper-based system. The system is dependent on the follow-up by the applicants. Any human error, such as an incorrect address declaration or a lost receipt, can lead to the disruption or complete halt of the entire process.

Mitigating Risks: Common Mistakes and Expert Advice

The residence permit application, due to its complex nature, can often invite errors. The most common mistakes and expert advice to avoid them are listed below:

  • Form Filling Errors: Using the wrong pen, illegible handwriting, or filling out incorrect sections can lead to the rejection of the application.

    • Advice: When filling out the application form, instructions must be strictly followed, and every piece of information must be meticulously checked.

  • Missing or Incorrect Documents: Forgetting a required document or submitting an incorrect one will cause the application to be stalled.

    • Advice: Before applying, every item on the document checklist mentioned above should be carefully checked, and it should be ensured that photocopies are complete.

  • Timing Errors: Especially in renewal applications, leaving procedures until the last minute can lead to serious problems. Considering the average processing time of 6 months, procedures should be started at least 4 months in advance.

    • Advice: Starting the application process as early as possible provides flexibility against unexpected delays.

The main points of failure in the process stem more from the applicant's carelessness than from systemic failures. Therefore, the most important variable for a successful application is the applicant's personal diligence and proactive follow-up.

Conclusion

The Permesso di Soggiorno application process can be easily managed with careful preparation, correct information, and a strategic approach. This report has detailed every step from the post office counter to the final card delivery. It is recommended that applicants break down the seemingly complex structure of the process into simple and manageable steps.

In conclusion, the three most important action items for a successful residence permit application are:

  1. Preparation: Prepare documents and forms completely, accurately, and in advance.

  2. Diligence: Pay attention to even the smallest detail when filling out the form and strictly follow the rules.

  3. Follow-up: Never lose the Ricevuta document after application, and meticulously track appointment dates.

With this approach, the application process can be successfully completed, and your educational life in Italy can be legally secured.

Special Cases in DSU Toscana Applications: Conditional Admission (Single Course) Master's 🎓

Many students, after applying for a master's degree in Italy, may face the condition of completing some undergraduate courses to be admitted to the program. The first question that comes to mind in this situation is:

👉 "Can conditionally admitted (single course) students apply for the DSU Toscana scholarship?"

Recent official answers provide clarity on this matter. Here are the details 👇

What is Conditional Admission (Single Course)?

  • You receive admission to a master's degree program (laurea magistrale) at a university.

  • However, direct enrollment is not possible due to missing courses (debito formativo).

  • To remedy these deficiencies, you can either take courses at a local university or complete the deficiencies by enrolling in "corsi singoli di transizione" (single course enrollment) at the University of Florence.

Is There a Right to Apply for DSU Toscana?

  • Single course students can also apply for the DSU scholarship.

  • Applications are evaluated under a “sospesa” (suspended/pending) status.

  • This means your right to the scholarship and accommodation appears on the lists, but it is not finalized.

When Does the Scholarship Become Active?

Your scholarship right becomes active when you complete the missing courses and register for your full-time master's degree.

  • If you fail to pass the courses before reaching this stage → the scholarship will be canceled, and you may need to reimburse for services received (dormitory, meals, etc.) (Art. 17.3 & Art. 22 provisions).

Summary of the Official Reply 📜

According to the answer from DSU:

  • Single course students can apply.

  • You can effectively use the scholarship once you complete your deficiencies and register for the regular program.

  • During this period, your scholarship will be "suspended."

  • However, for single course enrollment, it is essential to consult with the university's segreteria (student affairs office).

Recommendations for Students ✅

  • Definitely submit your application and get listed under "suspended" status.

  • Prioritize completing the missing courses.

  • Contact the segreteria to clarify the enrollment procedures.

  • Remember that if you cannot clear the deficiencies, you will lose your scholarship.

👉 Conditionally admitted (single course) students can apply for the DSU Toscana scholarship. However, the right to the scholarship is only finalized upon full-time master's degree enrollment.

So, there's no need to worry; submit your application. Just remember to complete the necessary courses at the end of the process.

54dcb767-a50c-4194-ad23-2dcc0850b6a4.excerpt: Residence Permit in Italy (“Permesso di Soggiorno”) | Step-by-Step Guide to Filling Out the Kit (Form) 📑🇮🇹 — For university-enrolment student visas in academic years 2026–2027 and

If you are studying in Italy as an Erasmus student, you must apply for a residence permit (Permesso di Soggiorno) within 8 working days after entering the country.For this application, you will use the so-called “Kit Giallo” (Yellow Kit), a packet containing the main forms: Modulo 1 and Modulo 2.

This guide explains how to correctly fill out Modulo 1, what documents to attach, and how the whole process works at the post office and the Questura (police headquarters).

General Rules and Important Notes

  • Pen: Use only a black ballpoint pen.

  • Writing: Fill out all fields in BLOCK LETTERS.

  • Leave blank: Skip the sections that do not apply to you.

  • Envelope: Do not seal the envelope – the postal clerk will do it.

Modulo 1 – Filling Guide (for Erasmus Students)

📄 Page 1 – Header and Sezione 1 & 2

  • Marca da Bollo: Stick it on the top right.

  • Codice Fiscale: Fill in if you already have one, otherwise leave blank.

  • Questura di: The name of the city where you apply (e.g., MILANO).

  • Provincia: Abbreviation of the province (e.g., MI).

  • Sezione 1 (Richiesta – Request):

    • Tick “Rilascio” (first issue).

    • Tick “Permesso di soggiorno”.

    • Motivo del rilascio/rinnovo → Write STUDIO (study).

    • Motivo specifico → Write ERASMUS.

    • Durata (mesi) → Duration of your Erasmus program (e.g., 6–12 months).

  • Sezione 2 (Application Details):

    • Complete this last.

    • “N. FOGLI”: Number of Modulo 1 pages (usually 4) + number of attached documents (passport copy, acceptance letter, etc.).

📄 Page 2 – Sezione 3 & 4 (Personal Data & Address in Italy)

Sezione 3 – Personal Data:

  • Cognome: Surname

  • Nome: First name

  • Sesso: M = Male, F = Female

  • Data di nascita: Date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY)

  • Stato di nascita: Country of birth (e.g., TURCHIA)

  • Cittadinanza: Citizenship (e.g., TURCA)

  • Codice Fiscale: If you have one, enter it

  • Stato civile: Marital status (S = Single, C = Married)

  • Nome Padre / Nome Madre: Optional, can be left blank

  • Passaporto N.: Passport number

  • Data rilascio: Date of issue

  • Valido fino al: Expiry date

  • Rilasciato da: Issuing authority (e.g., TURKEY)

  • Tipo documento: Tick “Passaporto”

Sezione 4 – Address in Italy:

  • Provincia: Province abbreviation (e.g., MI)

  • Comune: City (e.g., MILANO)

  • CAP: Postal code

  • Tipo via/piazza: Street type (e.g., VIA)

  • Indirizzo: Street name

  • N. civico: House number

  • Scala / Interno / Piano: Staircase, apartment, floor (if applicable)

  • Telefono: Italian phone number

  • Email: Email address

  • Tick the box to receive all communications at this address

📄 Page 3 – Sezione 5 & 6

Sezione 5 – Previous Residence Permits:

  • For renewals only → Leave blank for first-time Erasmus applicants

Sezione 6 – Reason for Stay:

  • Motivo del soggiorno: Write STUDIO

  • Tipo di studio: Write CORSO UNIVERSITARIO or ERASMUS

  • Nome Università: Name of your Italian university

  • Indirizzo Università: University address

  • Data inizio corso / Data fine corso: Start and end dates (from your acceptance letter)

  • N. iscrizione: Student registration number (if available, otherwise leave blank)

  • Stato di avanzamento: Tick Primo Anno (first year)

📄 Page 4 – Sezione 7

Sezione 7 – Declarations & Signatures:

  • Tick the declaration box

  • Luogo e Data: Place and date of application

  • Firma del Richiedente: Your signature

Modulo 2

  • Generally not required for Erasmus students.

  • Used mainly for work permits or complex financial situations

Required Supporting Documents (Photocopies)

  • Passport (ID page + visa page)

  • University Acceptance Letter

  • Health insurance valid in Italy

  • Proof of accommodation (rental contract or “Dichiarazione di Ospitalità”)

  • Codice Fiscale card (if available)

Post Office (Poste Italiane) Procedure

  1. Insert Modulo 1 and all copies into the Kit Giallo envelope (do not seal).

  2. Go to a Sportello Amico counter at any post office.

  3. Receive the Ricevuta (receipt) → very important, as it shows your Questura appointment.👉 This receipt is your temporary legal proof of residence in Italy until your card is issued.

Questura Appointment

  • Bring all original documents + 2 passport photos.

  • Your fingerprints will be taken.

  • The Questura will check your documents.

  • You will be notified (often by SMS) when your residence permit card is ready.

Conclusion

Applying for the Permesso di Soggiorno may seem complicated, but with the Kit Giallo the process is structured and manageable.👉 Follow the order: Fill out Modulo 1 → Attach documents → Post Office → Questura.

This way, you will be legally covered in Italy and can enjoy your Erasmus experience stress-free. 🇮🇹✨

d40a6435-22ab-4f5b-8ba3-0ab68c0c1c51.title: Curiosities About Erasmus
d40a6435-22ab-4f5b-8ba3-0ab68c0c1c51.excerpt: Curiosities About Erasmus — The Erasmus program is a European Union initiative that encourages higher education institutions in Europe to cooperate through student and staff exchange. The
d40a6435-22ab-4f5b-8ba3-0ab68c0c1c51.html:
The Erasmus program is a European Union initiative that encourages higher education institutions in Europe to cooperate through student and staff exchange. The program offers students and academic staff the opportunity to experience short-term education and training abroad. The program is named after the Dutch scholar Erasmus (1469-1536), one of the most important representatives of Renaissance Humanism.

1. What is the Erasmus Program?

Erasmus is a program that supports universities in Europe to cooperate, develop joint projects and exchange students and academics. Students can study abroad for a semester or a year and have the opportunity to learn about different cultures and gain international experience.

2. Is the Erasmus Program a Language Learning Program?

Erasmus is not a language learning program; however, students can study in a different country and have the opportunity to learn the language of that country. Students participating in the program can usually improve their language skills by attending language courses in the country they are going to.

3. Who can apply to the Erasmus Program?

To apply for the Erasmus program, you must be a student at a higher education institution. Applicants can study at a university that has an Erasmus agreement with their department. In addition, the academic achievements and language proficiency of the applicants are taken into consideration.

4. How Long Can Students Stay Abroad Under the Erasmus Program?

The student exchange period in the Erasmus program varies between 3 and 12 months. This period is compatible with student exchange programs and students can study at a contracted university abroad during this period.

5. What is the Application Process for the Erasmus Program?

Students who wish to apply for the Erasmus program must first contact the Erasmus coordinator at their university. The application process is usually evaluated on criteria such as academic achievement, language proficiency and motivation letter. Application periods are announced in the Fall and Spring semesters in accordance with the academic calendar.

6. How is Erasmus Grant and Financial Support Provided?

Under the Erasmus program, students are provided with financial support during their studies. This grant helps the student to cover living expenses abroad, but may not cover all costs. Grants may vary depending on the country of destination.

7. What are the Academic and Social Opportunities for Erasmus Students Abroad?

Erasmus students can benefit from the same academic and social opportunities at their destination university as the students there. This ranges from laboratory facilities to social activities. They may have to pay additional fees for some services, but in general they are provided with the same facilities.

8. How to Obtain a Passport and Visa as an Erasmus Student?

Students going abroad as part of the Erasmus program must organize their own passport and visa procedures. Visa procedures must be done in coordination with the consulate of the destination country.

9. Language Education and Preparatory Courses to be taken under the Erasmus Program

Erasmus students can attend language preparation courses to master the language of the destination country. These courses are organized for the student to improve their language skills before starting their academic studies.

10. How is the Erasmus grant received and when is it paid?

The Erasmus grant is paid partially in advance before the student goes abroad and the remaining part is paid after the study abroad is completed and the necessary documents are submitted. This payment process is carried out by the external relations offices of the universities.

The Erasmus program offers students the opportunity to gain international experience, get to know different cultures and contribute to their personal development. To make the most of the program, students should carefully follow the application process and make the necessary preparations in advance.

11. What is the Education and Tuition at the University of Erasmus Program?

Students who go abroad under the Erasmus program continue to enroll in their home universities and pay their tuition fees to their home universities. They do not have to pay any extra tuition fees at the destination university, which is one of the important advantages of the Erasmus program. However, in some cases small registration fees or other service fees may be charged.

12. Do Loans and Scholarships from the Credit and Dormitories Institution continue?

Students who are accepted to the Erasmus program do not lose their loans and scholarships from the Credit and Dormitories Institution. The Erasmus program offers support with an extra grant without interrupting the student's existing financial support. This allows students to have a more economically comfortable experience.

13. How are Passport and Visa Procedures for Erasmus Program?

Erasmus students must organize their own passport and visa procedures to go abroad. Visa procedures may vary depending on the country of destination. Therefore, students are advised to start their visa application process early and prepare the necessary documents in full.

14. Accommodation and Housing Opportunities at the University of Study

Erasmus students can receive support in finding accommodation at their host universities, but there is no strict obligation to do so. Many universities offer dormitories for Erasmus students, while some offer private rented housing options. Students need to research their accommodation options and book early.

15. How and when to get an Erasmus grant?

Grants under the Erasmus program are paid a certain percentage before students go abroad, and the remaining part is paid after students return and complete the necessary documents. This grant helps the student to cover living expenses abroad, but it may not be fully sufficient. Therefore, students should also consider finding additional sources of funding.

16. Participation in the Orientation Program Abroad as an Erasmus Student

Erasmus students usually attend orientation programs at their host universities. These programs make it easier for students to adapt to their new environment and provide information about the academic and social opportunities at the university. Orientation programs often also provide information about the local culture.

17. Utilizing Academic and Social Opportunities at the University of Study

Erasmus students can benefit from all academic and social opportunities offered by the host university on an equal basis with local students. Facilities such as laboratories, libraries and sports facilities are also open to Erasmus students. However, they may have to pay extra for some services.

18. Erasmus Grant Amount and Changes by Country

The amount of the grant given under the Erasmus program may vary depending on the country of destination. Although the grant provides support to cover the student's living expenses, it may not cover all costs. Students should make additional financial planning, taking into account the grant amount and country costs.

19. Language Preparation Courses and Academic Training for Erasmus Students

Erasmus students can attend pre-study language preparation courses in their destination country. These courses are important for students to continue their academic studies more efficiently in the local language. Language courses are usually organized by the university and tailored to the language level of the student.

20. Which documents are needed to apply for the Erasmus Program?

When applying for the Erasmus program, documents such as an application form, transcript, letter of intent, copy of passport and language proficiency certificate (for example, TOEFL or IELTS) are required. In addition, additional documents may be requested according to department-specific requirements. Students need to submit these documents in full and on time.

21. What is the Language Proficiency Requirement for the Erasmus Program?

Students who will participate in the Erasmus program must have sufficient knowledge of the language used as the language of instruction in the destination country. Universities usually require language proficiency at level B2. Students should attach official exam results to their application to prove their language proficiency.

22. How are the courses taken as an Erasmus student counted at my home university?

In order for the courses taken under the Erasmus program to be considered equivalent to the courses at your home university, a learning agreement is made. This agreement shows the credits and contents of the courses at the destination university. Upon return, these courses are formalized with a certificate of academic recognition, which states which courses they correspond to at your home university.

23. What are the other financial supports other than Erasmus Grant?

Apart from the Erasmus grant, there are additional scholarships provided by various foundations, associations and government agencies. Also, students can earn additional income by working abroad. However, it is important to get the necessary permissions to work and balance working hours with the study program.

24. What are the Insurance Requirements for Students Participating in the Erasmus Program?

Students going abroad under the Erasmus program are required to have health insurance. The insurance ensures that students can benefit from health services during their time abroad. While some universities offer affordable insurance packages, students can also take out their insurance.

25. What can I do if I am not accepted to the Erasmus Program?

Students who are not accepted to the Erasmus program can reapply for the next cycle of the program. They can also research other international exchange programs or consider study abroad opportunities. The reasons for not being accepted should be learned and it should be aimed to eliminate these deficiencies in the next applications.

26. What should be considered when choosing the country of destination for the Erasmus Program?

Factors such as language, culture, education system, living costs and academic opportunities offered by the university should be taken into consideration when choosing the country to be visited within the scope of the Erasmus program. Students should make a choice that will support both their academic and personal development while choosing the most suitable country for them.

27. How Does the Application Process for the Erasmus Program Work?

The Erasmus application process is managed by the External Relations Office of the universities. The application process is usually announced in Fall and Spring semesters. Students fill in the application forms, collect the necessary documents and complete their applications on the specified dates. Applications are usually evaluated based on language proficiency, academic achievement and motivation.

28. Are there any extra education or internship opportunities under the Erasmus Program?

The Erasmus program offers opportunities not only for course training but also for internships. Within the scope of Erasmus Internship Mobility, students may have the opportunity to do an internship in an institution abroad. These internships help students gain professional experience and prepare them for the world of work.

29. What are the Social Activity and Cultural Exchange Opportunities for Erasmus Students?

Erasmus students can participate in social activities at the universities they attend and meet other Erasmus students from different cultures. Universities usually organize cultural trips, language exchange programs and various social activities to help students mingle.

30. What are the Career Opportunities and Advantages After Erasmus Program?

Students who participate in the Erasmus program add value to their CVs by gaining international experience. This experience provides an important advantage in job applications after graduation. The Erasmus program offers students the opportunity to improve their language skills, gain cultural awareness and build an international network.

31. What are the eligibility requirements for the Erasmus Program and in which cases are students disqualified?

To apply for the Erasmus program, there are criteria such as being a student, language proficiency and academic success. After being accepted to the Erasmus program, academic failure, student disciplinary problems or non-compliance with the rules may result in disqualification. Also, failure to fulfill certain obligations after receiving a grant may result in the student having to repay the grant.

32. How are living costs in the countries where students study in the Erasmus Program covered?

The Erasmus grant is awarded to help students cover living costs abroad. However, this grant may not cover all expenses. Students should gather information about living costs and plan according to their own budget. It may also be useful for students to apply for other scholarship programs or consider part-time job opportunities for additional financial support.

33. How to ensure that the courses and credits earned under the Erasmus Program are recognized in my home country?

Recognition of courses taken under the Erasmus program is achieved through a learning agreement, which specifies which courses will be recognized at the student's home university. This agreement is made before departure and is required for the courses to be recognized upon return. Students are required to complete and submit the necessary documents to the student affairs office for the recognition of credits upon return.

34. How does participating in the Erasmus Program affect students' academic performance?

Participating in the Erasmus program can positively affect students' academic performance. Being in a new academic environment, experiencing different educational methodologies, and gaining different perspectives contribute to students' academic development. However, adapting to a new environment and education system can also take time, so students need to keep their motivation high.

35. How will my graduation process be affected after the Erasmus Program?

The courses taken during the Erasmus program should be carefully selected to avoid any disruption to the student's graduation plan. Students should review their course plans with their advisors before departure and take the necessary precautions for the recognition of credits and the smooth progress of their graduation process.

36. How does participation in the Erasmus Program contribute to students' personal development?

The Erasmus program contributes to students' personal development in many ways. Living in a different culture, making new friends, gaining experience of living independently and improving language skills increase students' self-confidence. These experiences also help students stand out in the job search after graduation.

37. What are the differences in the courses studied and the evaluation systems applied in the Erasmus Program?

Students participating in the Erasmus program should be aware that the education system at the university they attend may be different from that in their home country. Assessment systems, course content, and teaching methods may differ. Therefore, students need to be prepared to adapt to the courses and exams.

38. What are the Possible Problems in the Erasmus Program and How to Deal with These Problems?

Students participating in the Erasmus program may face problems such as language barriers, cultural differences, loneliness or financial difficulties. To cope with these problems, it may be useful to make use of the support services offered by universities, join local student societies and communicate with other Erasmus students.

39. What are the support services offered to students during the Erasmus Program?

Erasmus students are offered various support services by the universities they attend. These include orientation programs, language courses, academic counseling, and psychological support services. By making use of these services, students can cope with the difficulties they face during the program.

40. How does participation in the Erasmus Program affect career opportunities after graduation?

Students participating in the Erasmus program gain a competitive advantage in the business world by gaining international experience. This program increases students' cultural awareness, improves their language skills and provides an international networking opportunity. Employers may prefer graduates with Erasmus experience because of their ability to adapt to different environments and their global perspective.
